=\prod_{p}\left(1+p^{-s}+O_{F,\chi}(p^{-1-s})\right). $$

Thus, we can see that the singular series will converge at $s=2$ and in fact the convergence is at the same rate as the zeta function. We can now estimate that

$$ \sum_{b\geq X}\mu^{2}(b)\cdot\frac{a_{b}}{b^{2}}\ll\frac{1}{X}. $$

Combining this with the earlier bounds, we get that:

$$ \frac{BL^{2}\log(B/tk)^{\rho_{\Delta,f}-2}(8\deg(F))^{\omega(k)}}{tk^{2}}\sum_{b\geq X}\frac{\mu^{2}(b)}{b}\cdot\prod_{i=1}^{r}\sum_{e_{i}\mid b}\mu^{2}(e_{i})(1\star\chi)(b^{\deg(F_{i})}/e_{i})\cdot\frac{(8\deg(F))^{\omega(e_{i})}}{e_{i}}\\
\ll\frac{BL^{2}\log(B/tk)^{\rho_{\Delta,f}-2}(8\deg(F))^{\omega(k)}}{tk^{2}X}. $$

∎

If we take $X=\log(B)^{10^{-7}}$ , we will get a sufficient error term for Propostion 5.11. So from now on, we assume that $b\leq\log(B)^{10^{-7}}$ . Again, we must track how all future error terms depend on $b$ , since it does grow with $B$ ; fortunately, since $b$ is small in comparison with $B$ , we can allow any reasonable polynomial dependency on $b$ .

We define a new function to be estimated for a fixed $b$ :

$$ S(n,\mathbf{a},\mathbf{c},\mathbf{k};b)=\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}(x,y)\in(B/tk)^{1/2}\mathcal{B}(\mathbf{x}_{0},L)\\
b\mid x,y\\
k_{i}c_{i}\mid F_{i}(x,y)\\
p_{q_{j}}(F(x,y)/c)=n_{j}\\
p_{\neg-\Delta}(F_{i}(x,y)/k_{i}c_{i})\equiv a_{i}\bmod-\Delta\end{subarray}}\prod_{i=1}^{r}(1\star\chi)(p_{\neg-\Delta}(F_{i}(x,y)/k_{i}c_{i})). $$

### 8.4. Expanding the Dirichlet convolution

In our final reduction, we will expand the Dirichlet convolution $(1\star\chi)(n)$ . We note that for $\mathbf{a}\bmod-\Delta$ with $\gcd(a_{i},-\Delta)=1$ and $p_{\neg-\Delta}(F_{i}(x,y)/k_{i}c_{i})\equiv a_{i}\bmod-\Delta$ ,

$$ \displaystyle(1\star\chi)(p_{\neg-\Delta}(F_{i}(x,y)/k_{i}c_{i})) \displaystyle=\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}d_{i}\mid p_{\neg-\Delta}(F_{i}(x,y)/k_{i}c_{i})\end{subarray}}\chi(d_{i}) \displaystyle=\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}d_{i}\mid p_{\neg-\Delta}(F_{i}(x,y)/k_{i}c_{i})\\
d_{i}\leq\sqrt{p_{\neg-\Delta}(F_{i}/k_{i}c_{i})}\end{subarray}}\chi(d_{i})+\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}d_{i}\mid p_{\neg-\Delta}(F_{i}(x,y)/k_{i}c_{i})\\
d_{i}\leq\sqrt{p_{\neg-\Delta}(F_{i}/k_{i}c_{i})}\end{subarray}}\chi(a_{i}/d_{i}) \displaystyle=(1+\chi(a_{i}))\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}d_{i}\mid p_{\neg-\Delta}(F_{i}(x,y)/k_{i}c_{i})\\
d_{i}\leq\sqrt{p_{\neg-\Delta}(F_{i}/k_{i}c_{i})}\end{subarray}}\chi(d_{i}). $$

We remark that if $p_{\neg-\Delta}(F_{i}(x,y)/k_{i}c_{i})$ is a square, then the second equality should be modified to be a sum over $d_{i}\leq\sqrt{p_{\neg-\Delta}}$ and $d_{i}<\sqrt{p_{\neg-\Delta}}.$ However, the contribution from those $(x,y)$ such that $p_{\neg-\Delta}(F_{i}(x,y)/k_{i}c_{i})$ is a square can be shown to be negligible via the large sieve. From now on, we ignore these terms. Let us define:

$$ S(n,\mathbf{a},\mathbf{c},\mathbf{k},b;\mathbf{d})=\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}(x,y)\in(B/tk)^{1/2}\mathcal{B}(\mathbf{x}_{0},L)\\
b\mid x,y\\
k_{i}c_{i}d_{i}\mid F_{i}(x,y)\\
p_{q_{j}}(F(x,y)/c)=n_{j}\\
p_{\neg-\Delta}(F_{i}(x,y)/k_{i}c_{i})\equiv a_{i}\bmod-\Delta\end{subarray}}1. $$

Then we can rewrite (8.5) as:

$$ S(n,\mathbf{a},\mathbf{c},\mathbf{k};b)=\prod_{i=1}^{r}(1+\chi(a_{i}))\sum_{d_{i}\leq\max_{(x,y)\in(B/tk)^{1/2}\mathcal{B}(\mathbf{x}_{0},L)}\sqrt{|F_{i}(x,y)|/n_{i}k_{i}c_{i}}}\prod_{i=1}^{r}\chi(d_{i})\cdot S(n,\mathbf{a},\mathbf{c},\mathbf{k},b;\mathbf{d}). $$

Our next goal is to establish either asymptotics on average or upper bounds for $S(n,\mathbf{a},\mathbf{c},\mathbf{k},b;\mathbf{d}).$ To do so, we will have different treatments for various ranges of $\mathbf{d}$ . For “small” $\mathbf{d}$ (the precise definition of this will be given in §11.1, as it depends on the factorization of $F(x,y)$ ), we use a level of distribution result established in §9 – this will provide our main term. For “large” $\mathbf{d}$ , we will prove upper bounds in §10 using Nair’s sieve that will go into our final error term.

#### Remark 8.7.

Since there are many variables in the final expression we wish to estimate $S(n,\mathbf{a},\mathbf{c},\mathbf{k};b)$ , let us remark now on their approximate “size” and what aspects need to be tracked throughout the following proof.

- • $n$ is a small constant ( $n\ll\log(B)^{10^{-7}}$ ; it also satisfies that $p\mid n\implies p\mid-\Delta$ and hence $\sum n^{-e}$ for any $e>0$ will converge to a constant only depending on $-\Delta$ . Its importance appears in the computations for evaluating the main term.

- • $\mathbf{a}$ appear with respect to congruences mod $n(-\Delta)$ . This aspect is a nuisance when establishing the error term but is relevant for evaluating the main term.

- • $\mathbf{c}$ has entries that must divide their respect resultants $\textrm{Res}(F_{i},F_{j})$ for $i\neq j$ . Since the pairwise resultants are fixed constants given a form $F$ , the dependency on $\mathbf{c}$ is not needed to be tracked for the error term. However, tracking the dependence on $\mathbf{c}$ is crucial for evaluating the main term. When $F$ is irreducible, it is not necessary to sum over $\mathbf{c}$ (i.e. $\mathbf{c}=1).$

- • $\mathbf{k}$ satisfies that $k\leq B/\exp(\sqrt{\log(B)})$ and its dependence must be tracked throughout the error term computations, as we later sum over $k$ (recall that by construction, for each $k$ there is a unique vector chosen as $\mathbf{k}$ ). It is not as relevant for the main term computation.

- • $b$ is a small constant $(b\leq\log(B)^{10^{-7}})$ and its dependence must be tracked throughout the error term computations. However, it is not particularly relevant for the main term computations.

## 9. Level of distribution

In this section, we will prove a level of distribution result for squarefree binary forms of degree $\leq 4$ alluded to in the paragraphs above. Let us write it out now in its full technical detail:

#### Proposition 9.1.

Let $F(x,y)=\prod_{i=1}^{r}F_{i}(x,y)$ be a squarefree binary form of degree $\leq 4$ , where $F_{i}(x,y)$ are irreducible factors of $F(x,y)$ . For a fixed $n,\mathbf{a},\mathbf{c},\mathbf{k},\mathbf{d}=(d_{i})$ and $b$ , we define the following local function:

$$ \varrho_{F}(\mathbf{d};b,n,\mathbf{a},\mathbf{c},\mathbf{k}):=\#\{\mathbf{x}\bmod bcdkn(-\Delta):k_{i}c_{i}d_{i}\mid F_{i}(x,y),b\mid\gcd(x,y),\\
p_{-\Delta}(F(x,y))=n,p_{\neg-\Delta}(F_{i}(x,y)/k_{i}c_{i})\equiv a_{i}\bmod-\Delta\}. $$

For a tuple $\mathbf{D}=(D_{i})_{i=1}^{r}$ , we define the error quantity as:

$$ E(\mathbf{D})=\sum_{d_{i}\sim D_{i}}\left|S(n,\mathbf{a},\mathbf{c},\mathbf{k},b;\mathbf{d})-\frac{\varrho_{F}(\mathbf{d};b,n,\mathbf{a},\mathbf{c},\mathbf{k})}{(bcdkn(-\Delta))^{2}}\cdot\frac{BL^{2}}{tk}\right|. $$

Let $D=D_{1}\dots D_{r}$ . If $F(x,y)$ has no linear factors, then we have that for an explicit constant $\gamma_{r}>0$ , the following bound holds:

$$ E(\mathbf{D})\ll\frac{\varrho_{F}^{*}(\mathbf{k})\tau(k)}{\varphi(k)}\cdot D\cdot\log\left(1+\frac{BL^{2}}{tkD}\right)^{9}+\frac{64^{\omega(k)}}{k}\cdot\frac{D}{b^{2}}\cdot\exp(\gamma_{r}\sqrt{\log_{2}(B/tk)\log_{3}(B/tk)})\\
+\frac{B^{1/2}L}{t^{1/2}}\cdot\frac{64^{\omega(k)}}{k}\cdot\frac{\tau(b^{4})}{b}\cdot\sqrt{D}\cdot\exp(\gamma_{r}\sqrt{\log_{2}(kcD)\log_{3}(kcD)}). $$

If $F(x,y)$ has a linear factor, then we have that

$$ E(\mathbf{D})\ll\frac{\varrho_{F}^{*}(\mathbf{k})\tau(k)}{\varphi(k)}\cdot D\cdot\log\left(1+\frac{BL^{2}}{tkD}\right)^{9}+\frac{64^{\omega(k)}}{k}\cdot\frac{D}{b^{2}}\cdot\exp(\gamma_{r}\sqrt{\log_{2}(B/tk)\log_{3}(B/tk)})\\
+\frac{B^{1/2}L}{t^{1/2}}\cdot\frac{64^{\omega(k)}}{k}\cdot\frac{\tau(b^{4})}{b}\cdot\sqrt{D}\cdot\exp(\gamma_{r}\sqrt{\log_{2}(kcD)\log_{3}(kcD)})\\
+\frac{B^{1/2}L}{(tk)^{1/2}}\cdot\frac{1}{b}\cdot\max_{i:\deg(F_{i})=1}D_{i}\log(kcD)^{2}\log\left(1+\frac{BL^{2}}{tkD}\right)^{8}. $$

#### Remark 9.2.

The constant $\gamma_{r}$ is worked out explicitly in the work of Hall and Tenenbaum [31] on generalized Hooley’s $\Delta$ -functions.

Our proof when $F(x,y)$ has no linear factors follows the proof of the level of distribution result written in de la Bretèche and Tenenbaum in [25]. In this case, the level of distribution is near optimal in the sense that we can take $D\leq\frac{BL^{2}}{tk}\log(B)^{-\epsilon}$ for any $\epsilon>0$ ; in other words, we can let $\epsilon$ be very small, such as $10^{-5}$ . If $F(x,y)$ has linear factors, then we get a slightly worse level of distribution result – we will need $D_{i}\leq\frac{BL^{2}}{tk}\log(B)^{-1-\epsilon}$ in the final term. Luckily, our results for large moduli are more flexible in this case. We also would like to point out the work of Marasingha [39] towards level of distribution results for arbitrary squarefree binary forms.

### 9.1. Lattices of $F(x,y)$

First, we will explore the distribution of lattices corresponding to the divisors of $F(x,y)$ and how they connect to our error term. We start by fixing a tuple $\mathbf{d}=(d_{i})_{i=1}^{r}$ . For a collection of squarefree binary forms $F_{1}(x,y),...,F_{k}(x,y)$ , we define the following divisor lattices:

$$ \Lambda(d_{1},...,d_{k}):=\{(x,y)\in\mathbb{Z}^{2}:d_{i}\mid F_{i}(x,y)\}. $$

$$ \Lambda(d_{1},...,d_{k};b):=\{(x,y)\in\mathbb{Z}^{2}:d_{i}\mid F_{i}(x,y),b\mid x,y\}. $$

It is noteworthy that these will be the union of lattices of determinant $d_{1}...d_{n}$ or $b^{2}d_{1}...d_{n}$ ; this observation was made by Daniel in [18]. From now on, we use the shorthand notation:

$$ \Lambda(\mathbf{c}\mathbf{k}\mathbf{d};b):=\Lambda(c_{1}k_{1}d_{1},\ldots,c_{r}k_{r}d_{r};b). $$

We also will want to consider the lattice:

$$ \Lambda^{*}(d_{1},\dots,d_{k};b)=\{(x,y)\in\mathbb{Z}^{2}:d_{i}\mid F_{i}(x,y),b\mid\gcd(x,y),\gcd(x,y,d)=1\}. $$

Similarly, we use the shorthand notation that

$$ \Lambda^{*}(\mathbf{c}\mathbf{k}\mathbf{d};b):=\Lambda^{*}(c_{1}k_{1}d_{1},\dots,c_{r}k_{r}d_{r};b). $$

Next, we further decompose $\Lambda(\mathbf{c}\mathbf{k}\mathbf{d};b)$ and $\Lambda^{*}(\mathbf{c}\mathbf{k}\mathbf{d};b)$ into lattices corresponding to solutions of $F_{i}(x,y)\bmod k_{i}c_{i}d_{i}$ . Let $\alpha=(\alpha_{1},\alpha_{2})$ satisfy that $F_{i}(\alpha)\equiv 0\bmod k_{i}c_{i}d_{i}$ for all $i$ , $b\mid\alpha_{1},\alpha_{2}$ and that $\gcd(\alpha_{1},\alpha_{2},kcd)=1.$ Then we define

$$ \Lambda(\alpha;ckd,b):=\{\mathbf{x}\in\mathbb{Z}^{2}:\mathbf{x}\equiv\lambda\alpha\bmod bcdk\text{ for some $\lambda\in\mathbb{Z}$}\}. $$

It follows that $\Lambda(\alpha;ckd,b)$ is a lattice with determinant $b^{2}cdk$ . We will also consider

$$ \Lambda^{*}(\alpha;ckd;b):=\{(x,y)\in\mathbb{Z}^{2}:(x,y)\equiv\lambda\alpha\bmod bcdk,\gcd(x,y,ckd)=1\}. $$

Let us write

$$ \mathcal{U}(\mathbf{c}\mathbf{k}\mathbf{d};b)=\{\alpha\bmod bcdk:F_{i}(\alpha)\equiv 0\bmod k_{i}c_{i}d_{i},b\mid(\alpha_{1},\alpha_{2}),\gcd(\alpha_{1},\alpha_{2},kcd)=1\}/\sim, $$

where equivalence is defined as $\alpha\sim\alpha^{\prime}$ if and only if $\alpha=\lambda\alpha^{\prime}\bmod kcd$ for $\lambda\neq 0$ . Then we can see that

$$ \#(B/tk)^{1/2}\mathcal{B}(\mathbf{x}_{0},L)\cap\Lambda^{*}(\mathbf{c}\mathbf{k}\mathbf{d};b)=\sum_{\alpha\in\mathcal{U}(\mathbf{c}\mathbf{k}\mathbf{d};b)}\#(B/tk)^{1/2}\mathcal{B}(\mathbf{x}_{0},L)\cap\Lambda^{*}(\alpha;ckd,b). $$

We also must specify the conditions that $p_{-\Delta}(F(x,y)/c)=n$ and $p_{\neg-\Delta}(F_{i}(x,y)/k_{i}c_{i})\equiv a_{i}\bmod-\Delta$ . Define

$$ \Lambda(n,\mathbf{a}):=\{\mathbf{x}\in\mathbb{Z}^{2}:p_{-\Delta}(F(x,y)/c)=n,p_{\neg-\Delta}(F_{i}(x,y)/k_{i}c_{i})\equiv a_{i}\bmod-\Delta\}. $$

Observe that the above is not a lattice, despite the notation, but is still defined by congruence conditions mod $n(-\Delta)$ in $\mathbb{Z}^{2}$ and will be the shift of a finite union of lattices with determinant $n^{2}(-\Delta)^{2}$ . Then, we can see that we would like to count in Proposition 9.1

$$ \#(B/tk)^{1/2}\mathcal{B}(\mathbf{x}_{0},L)\cap\Lambda(\mathbf{c}\mathbf{k}\mathbf{d};b)\cap\Lambda(n,\mathbf{a}). $$

It will be advantageous for us to first consider

$$ \#(B/tk)^{1/2}\mathcal{B}(\mathbf{x}_{0},L)\cap\Lambda^{*}(\mathbf{c}\mathbf{k}\mathbf{d};b)\cap\Lambda(n,\mathbf{a})=\sum_{\alpha\in\mathcal{U}(\mathbf{c}\mathbf{k}\mathbf{d};b)}\#(B/tk)^{1/2}\mathcal{B}(\mathbf{x}_{0},L)\cap\Lambda^{*}(\alpha;ckd;b)\cap\Lambda(n,\mathbf{a}). $$

### 9.2. A step along the way

We first want to consider following sum:

$$ S^{*}(n,\mathbf{a},\mathbf{c},\mathbf{k},b;\mathbf{d}):=\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}(x,y)\in(B/tk)^{1/2}\mathcal{B}(\mathbf{x}_{0},L)\\
b\mid x,y\\
k_{i}c_{i}d_{i}\mid F_{i}(x,y)\\
p_{-\Delta}(F(x,y)/c)=n\\
p_{\neg-\Delta}(F_{i}(x,y)/k_{i}c_{i})\equiv a_{i}\bmod-\Delta\end{subarray}}\mathbf{1}_{\gcd(x,y,kcd)=1}. $$

We also define the corresponding local counting function

$$ \varrho^{*}_{F}(\mathbf{d};b,n,\mathbf{a},\mathbf{c},\mathbf{k}):=\#\{\mathbf{x}\bmod bcdkn(-\Delta):k_{i}c_{i}d_{i}\mid F_{i}(x,y),\gcd(x,y,kcd)=1,\\
b\mid(x,y),p_{-\Delta}(F(x,y)/c)=n,p_{\neg-\Delta}(F_{i}(x,y)/k_{i}c_{i})\equiv a_{i}\bmod-\Delta\}. $$

Another way to view this count $\varrho^{*}_{F}(\mathbf{d};b,n,\mathbf{a},\mathbf{c},\mathbf{k})$ is that it is $\varphi(kcd)\cdot\#\mathcal{U}(\mathbf{c}\mathbf{k}\mathbf{d};b)$ multiplied against the number of lattices of determinant $n^{2}(-\Delta)^{2}$ in $\Lambda(n,\mathbf{a}).$ First, we will establish that the following lattice counting result.

#### Lemma 9.3.

Let $F(x,y)=\prod_{i=1}^{r}F_{i}(x,y)$ be a squarefree binary form of degree $\leq 4$ , where $F_{i}(x,y)$ are irreducible factors of $F(x,y).$ For a fixed $n,\mathbf{a},\mathbf{c},\mathbf{k}$ , and a tuple $\mathbf{D}=(D_{i})_{i=1}^{r}$ , we define the error quantity:

$$ E^{*}(\mathbf{D})=\sum_{d_{i}\sim D_{i}}\left|S^{*}(n,\mathbf{a},\mathbf{c},\mathbf{k},b;\mathbf{d})-\frac{\varrho_{F}^{*}(\mathbf{d};b,n,\mathbf{a},\mathbf{c},\mathbf{k})}{(cdbn(-\Delta))^{2}}\cdot\frac{BL^{2}}{tk^{3}}\right|. $$

Let $D=D_{1}\dots D_{r}$ . If $F(x,y)$ has no linear factors, then there is an explicit constant $\gamma_{r}>0$ such that

$$ E^{*}(\mathbf{D})\ll_{\Delta,f}\frac{\varrho_{F}^{*}(\mathbf{k})\tau(k)}{\varphi(k)}\cdot D\cdot\left(1+\log\left(\frac{BL^{2}}{tk^{2}cb^{2}(n(-\Delta))^{2}D}\right)\right)\\
+\frac{B^{1/2}L}{t^{1/2}}\cdot\frac{64^{\omega(k)}}{k}\cdot\frac{\tau(b^{4})}{b}\cdot\sqrt{D}\cdot\exp(\gamma_{r}\sqrt{\log_{2}(kcD)\log_{3}(kcD)}). $$

If $F(x,y)$ has a linear factor, then we have that

$$ E^{*}(\mathbf{D})\ll_{\Delta,f}\frac{\varrho_{F}^{*}(\mathbf{k})\tau(k)}{\varphi(k)}\cdot D\cdot\left(1+\log\left(\frac{BL^{2}}{tk^{2}cb^{2}(n(-\Delta))^{2}D}\right)\right)\\
+\frac{B^{1/2}L}{t^{1/2}}\cdot\frac{64^{\omega(k)}}{k}\cdot\frac{\tau(b^{4})}{b}\cdot\sqrt{D}\cdot\exp(\gamma_{r}\sqrt{\log_{2}(kcD)\log_{3}(kcD)})\\
+\frac{B^{1/2}L}{(tk)^{1/2}}\cdot\frac{1}{b}\cdot\max_{i:\deg(F_{i})=1}D_{i}\log(kcD)^{2}. $$

#### Proof.

The proof of the lemma above will eventually split into two cases: when $F(x,y)$ contains a linear factor and when it does not (which is equivalent to when $F(x,y)$ has a nontrivial integral solution and when it does not). However, the starting step for both cases is the same.

Since we have definitionally the relation that

$$ S^{*}(n,\mathbf{a},\mathbf{c},\mathbf{k},b;\mathbf{d})=\#(B/tk)^{1/2}\mathcal{B}(\mathbf{x}_{0},L)\cap\Lambda^{*}(\mathbf{c}\mathbf{k}\mathbf{d};b)\cap\Lambda(n,\mathbf{a})\\
=\sum_{\alpha\in\mathcal{U}(\mathbf{c}\mathbf{k}\mathbf{d};b)}\#(B/tk)^{1/2}\mathcal{B}(\mathbf{x}_{0},L)\cap\Lambda^{*}(\alpha;ckd;b)\cap\Lambda(n,\mathbf{a})\\
=\sum_{\alpha\in\mathcal{U}(\mathbf{c}\mathbf{k}\mathbf{d};b)}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}\mathbf{x}^{\prime}\bmod n(-\Delta)\\
p_{-\Delta}(F(x,y)/c)=n\\
p_{\neg-\Delta}(F_{i}(x,y)/k_{i}c_{i})\equiv a_{i}\bmod-\Delta\end{subarray}}\#(B/tk)^{1/2}\mathcal{B}(\mathbf{x}_{0},L)\cap\Lambda^{*}(\alpha;ckd;b)\cap\Lambda(\mathbf{x}^{\prime};n(-\Delta)), $$

where the “shifted lattice”, $\Lambda(\mathbf{x}^{\prime};n(-\Delta))$ , is of determinant $n^{2}(-\Delta)^{2}$ and given by

$$ \Lambda(\mathbf{x}_{0};n(-\Delta))=\{x,y\in\mathbb{Z}^{2}:(x,y)\equiv\mathbf{x}^{\prime}\bmod n(-\Delta)\}. $$

Next, by Möbius inversion,

$$ \Lambda^{*}(\alpha,ckd;b)=\sum_{g\mid ckd}\mu(g)\#\{g\mathbf{x}\in\Lambda(\alpha;ckd;b)\}. $$

Hence, we have that $S^{*}(n,\mathbf{a},\mathbf{c},\mathbf{k},b;\mathbf{d})$ becomes

$$ =\sum_{g\mid ckd}\mu(g)\sum_{\alpha\in\mathcal{U}(\mathbf{c}\mathbf{k}\mathbf{d};b)}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}\mathbf{x}^{\prime}\bmod n(-\Delta)\\
p_{-\Delta}(F(x,y)/c)=n\\
p_{\neg-\Delta}(F_{i}(x,y)/k_{i}c_{i})\equiv a_{i}\bmod-\Delta\end{subarray}}\#\frac{1}{g}(B/tk)^{1/2}\mathcal{B}(\mathbf{x}_{0},L)\cap\Lambda(\alpha;ckd/g;b);\cap\Lambda(\mathbf{x}^{\prime};n(-\Delta)). $$

Now, by standard lattice counting arguments, we have that

$$ \#\frac{1}{g}(B/tk)^{1/2}\mathcal{B}(\mathbf{x}_{0},L)\cap\Lambda(\alpha;ckd/g;b)\cap\Lambda(\mathbf{x}^{\prime};n(-\Delta))=\frac{BL^{2}}{tkg^{2}}\cdot\frac{g}{ckdb^{2}}\cdot\frac{1}{(n(-\Delta))^{2}}\\
+O\left(\frac{B^{1/2}L}{(tk)^{1/2}g}\cdot\frac{1}{\lambda_{1}(\Lambda(\alpha;ckd/g;b)\cap\Lambda(\mathbf{x}^{\prime};n(-\Delta)))}\right)+O\left(\min\left(1,\frac{BL^{2}}{gtk^{2}cdb^{2}(n(-\Delta))^{2}}\right)\right), $$

where $\lambda_{1}(\Lambda)$ denotes the first successive minima of a lattice (see [25, p. 773]).

First, we consider the main term:

$$ \frac{BL^{2}}{tk^{2}}\cdot\frac{1}{ckdb^{2}n(-\Delta)^{2}}\cdot\sum_{\alpha\in\mathcal{U}(\mathbf{c}\mathbf{k}\mathbf{d};b)}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}\mathbf{x}^{\prime}\bmod n(-\Delta)\\
p_{-\Delta}(F(x,y)/c)=n\\
p_{\neg-\Delta}(F_{i}(x,y)/k_{i}c_{i})\equiv a_{i}\bmod-\Delta\end{subarray}}\sum_{g\mid ckd}\frac{\mu(g)}{g}\\
=\frac{BL^{2}}{tk^{2}}\cdot\frac{1}{ckdb^{2}(n(-\Delta))^{2}}\cdot\sum_{\alpha\in\mathcal{U}(\mathbf{c}\mathbf{k}\mathbf{d};b)}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}\mathbf{x}^{\prime}\bmod n(-\Delta)\\
p_{-\Delta}(F(x,y)/c)=n\\
p_{\neg-\Delta}(F_{i}(x,y)/k_{i}c_{i})\equiv a_{i}\bmod-\Delta\end{subarray}}\frac{\varphi(ckd)}{ckd}. $$

Since $\varrho_{F}^{*}(\mathbf{d};b,n,\mathbf{a},\mathbf{c},\mathbf{k})$ is exactly $\varphi(ckd)$ times the count being summed over, this gives that

$$ E^{*}(D)\ll\Sigma_{1}+\Sigma_{2}, $$

where we take

$$ \Sigma_{1}=\sum_{d_{i}\sim D_{i}}\sum_{g\mid ckd}\sum_{\alpha\in\mathcal{U}(\mathbf{c}\mathbf{k}\mathbf{d};b)}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}\mathbf{x}^{\prime}\bmod n(-\Delta)\\
p_{-\Delta}(F(x,y)/c)=n\\
p_{\neg-\Delta}(F_{i}(x,y)/k_{i}c_{i})\equiv a_{i}\bmod-\Delta\end{subarray}}\frac{B^{1/2}L}{(tk)^{1/2}g}\cdot\frac{1}{\lambda_{1}(\Lambda(\alpha;ckd/g;b)\cap\Lambda(\mathbf{x}^{\prime};n(-\Delta)))} $$

and

$$ \Sigma_{2}=\sum_{d_{i}\sim D_{i}}\sum_{g\mid ckd}\sum_{\alpha\in\mathcal{U}(\mathbf{c}\mathbf{k}\mathbf{d};b)}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}\mathbf{x}^{\prime}\bmod n(-\Delta)\\
p_{-\Delta}(F(x,y)/c)=n\\
p_{\neg-\Delta}(F_{i}(x,y)/k_{i}c_{i})\equiv a_{i}\bmod-\Delta\end{subarray}}\min\left(1,\frac{BL^{2}}{gtk^{2}cdb^{2}(n(-\Delta))^{2}}\right). $$

First, let us treat the second term $\Sigma_{2}$ . First, we observe that the number of $\mathbf{x}^{\prime}\bmod n(-\Delta)$ such that $p_{-\Delta}(F(x,y)/c)=n$ and $p_{\neg-\Delta}(F_{i}(x,y)/k_{i}c_{i})\equiv a_{i}\bmod-\Delta$ is $O_{\Delta}(1)$ . So, we can safely ignore this summand and see that

$$ \Sigma_{2}\ll_{\Delta}\sum_{d_{i}\sim D_{i}}\sum_{g\mid cdk}\frac{\varrho^{*}_{F}(\mathbf{d};b,n,\mathbf{a},\mathbf{c},\mathbf{k})}{\varphi(ckd)}\min\left(1,\frac{BL^{2}}{gtk^{2}cdb^{2}(n(-\Delta))^{2}}\right). $$

We make the observation that

$$ \varrho_{F}^{*}(\mathbf{d};b,n,\mathbf{a},\mathbf{c},\mathbf{k})\ll_{\Delta}\varrho_{F}^{*}(\mathbf{d};1,1,\mathbf{0},1,\mathbf{k})=\varrho_{F}^{*}(\mathbf{d}\mathbf{k}). $$

Since $c$ can be treated as a constant and because $\varrho_{F}^{*}$ is a submultiplicative function, it suffices to understand:

$$ \sum_{h\mid k}\frac{\varrho_{F}^{*}(\mathbf{k})}{\varphi(k)}\sum_{d_{i}\sim D_{i}}\sum_{g\mid d}\frac{\varrho^{*}_{F}(\mathbf{d})}{\varphi(d)}\min\left(1,\frac{BL^{2}}{hgtk^{2}cdb^{2}(n(-\Delta))^{2}}\right) $$

We split up the sum by the contribution when $g\cdot d>\frac{BL^{2}}{htk^{2}cb^{2}(n(-\Delta))^{2}}$ , denoted as $\Sigma_{2}^{*}$ , and otherwise, denoted as $\Sigma_{2}^{**}$ . In the first setting, we have that

$$ \Sigma_{2}^{*}\ll_{\Delta}\frac{BL^{2}}{tk^{2}cb^{2}(n(-\Delta))^{2}}\sum_{h\mid k}\frac{\varrho_{F}^{*}(\mathbf{k})}{\varphi(k)h}\sum_{g>\frac{BL^{2}}{htk^{2}cb^{2}(n(-\Delta))^{2}D}}\frac{1}{g}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}d_{i}\sim D_{i}\\
g\mid d\\
d>\frac{BL^{2}}{hgtk^{2}cb^{2}(n(-\Delta))^{2}}\end{subarray}}\frac{\varrho_{F}^{*}(\mathbf{d})}{\varphi(d)d}.\\
\ll_{\Delta}\frac{BL^{2}}{tk^{2}cb^{2}n^{2}}\sum_{h\mid k}\frac{\varrho_{F}^{*}(\mathbf{k})}{\varphi(k)h}\sum_{g>\frac{BL^{2}}{htk^{2}cb^{2}(n(-\Delta))^{2}D}}\frac{\varrho_{F}^{*}(\mathbf{g})}{\varphi(g)g^{2}}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}d_{i}^{\prime}\sim D_{i}/g_{i}\\
d^{\prime}>\frac{BL^{2}}{g^{2}htk^{2}cb^{2}(n(-\Delta))^{2}}\end{subarray}}\frac{\varrho^{*}_{F}(\mathbf{d}^{\prime})}{\varphi(d^{\prime})d^{\prime}}. $$

Above we have used the following properties: the local counting function $\varrho_{F}^{*}$ is sub-multiplicative; we have already seen that although we must divide $g=g_{1}\dots g_{r}$ where $g_{i}\mid d_{i}$ for each $i$ , there are only finitely many such decompositions as any value $g$ such that $g_{i}\mid F_{i}(x,y)$ (as common divisors must divide $\textrm{Res}(F_{i},F_{j})$ ) and we choose a decomposition arbitrarily above.

Thus, it suffices to understand the sum

$$ \sum_{d^{\prime}\in[D^{1},D^{2}]}\frac{\varrho^{*}_{F}(\mathbf{d}^{\prime})}{\varphi(d^{\prime})d^{\prime}}. $$

We observe that the Dirichlet series

$$ \xi(s;F)=\sum_{\mathbf{d}}\frac{\varrho_{F}^{*}(\mathbf{d};\mathbf{1})}{\varphi(d)d^{s}} $$

has the same analytic behavior as the product of $L$ -functions

$$ \prod_{i=1}^{r}\zeta_{\mathbb{Q}[z]/f_{i}(z)}(s) $$

as $s\rightarrow 1^{+}$ . Hence, this gives us that

$$ \sum_{d^{\prime}\in[D^{1},D^{2}]}\frac{\varrho_{F}^{*}(d^{\prime};\mathbf{1})}{\varphi(d^{\prime})d^{\prime}}\ll_{\Delta,f}\log(D^{2}/D^{1})^{r}+1. $$

With the above identity in-hand, and noting that we sum $d_{i}$ in a dyadic interval, we can see that

$$ \Sigma_{2}^{*}\ll_{\Delta,f}\frac{BL^{2}}{tk^{2}cb^{2}n^{2}}\cdot\sum_{h\mid k}\frac{\varrho_{F}^{*}(\mathbf{k})}{\varphi(k)h}\sum_{g>\frac{BL^{2}}{htk^{2}cb^{2}(n(-\Delta))^{2}D}}\frac{\varrho_{F}^{*}(\mathbf{g})}{\varphi(g)g^{2}}\\
\ll_{\Delta,f}\frac{BL^{2}}{tk^{2}cb^{2}n^{2}}\cdot\sum_{h\mid k}\frac{\varrho_{F}^{*}(\mathbf{k})}{\varphi(k)h}\cdot\frac{htk^{2}cb^{2}(n(-\Delta))^{2}D}{BL^{2}}\ll_{\Delta,f}\frac{\varrho_{F}^{*}(\mathbf{k})\tau(k)}{\varphi(k)}\cdot D. $$

Here we have use that

$$ \sum_{\mathbf{d}}\frac{\varrho_{F}^{*}(\mathbf{d})}{\varphi(d)d^{2}} $$

will converge absolutely and at the same rate that $\prod_{i=1}^{r}\zeta_{\mathbb{Q}[z]/f_{i}(z)}(2)$ converges.

For $\Sigma_{2}^{**}$ , we proceed with the opposite contribution:

$$ \Sigma_{2}^{**}\ll_{\Delta}\sum_{h\mid k}\frac{\varrho_{F}^{*}(\mathbf{k})}{\varphi(k)}\sum_{d_{i}\sim D_{i}}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}g\mid d\\
g\leq\frac{BL^{2}}{htk^{2}cb^{2}(n(-\Delta))^{2}D}\end{subarray}}\frac{\varrho_{F}^{*}(\mathbf{d})}{\varphi(d)}\\
\ll_{\Delta}\sum_{h\mid k}\frac{\varrho_{F}^{*}(\mathbf{k})}{\varphi(k)}\sum_{g\leq\frac{BL^{2}}{htk^{2}cb^{2}(n(-\Delta))^{2}D}}\frac{\varrho_{F}^{*}(\mathbf{g})}{\varphi(g)}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}d_{i}\sim D_{i}/g_{i}\end{subarray}}\frac{\varrho_{F}^{*}(\mathbf{d}^{\prime})}{\varphi(d^{\prime})}. $$

Again, let us use the analytic properties of $\xi(s;F)$ to evaluate the summands:

$$ \Sigma_{2}^{**}\ll_{\Delta,f}\sum_{h\mid k}\frac{\varrho_{F}^{*}(\mathbf{k})}{\varphi(k)}\cdot D\cdot\sum_{g\leq\frac{BL^{2}}{htk^{2}cb^{2}(n(-\Delta))^{2}D}}\frac{\varrho_{F}^{*}(\mathbf{g})}{\varphi(g)g}\ll_{\Delta,f}\sum_{h\mid k}\frac{\varrho_{F}^{*}(\mathbf{k})}{\varphi(k)}\cdot D\cdot\log\left(\frac{BL^{2}}{htk^{2}cb^{2}(n(-\Delta))^{2}D}\right)\\
\ll_{\Delta,f}\frac{\varrho_{F}^{*}(\mathbf{k})\tau(k)}{\varphi(k)}\cdot D\cdot\log\left(\frac{BL^{2}}{tk^{2}cb^{2}(n(-\Delta))^{2}D}\right). $$

Together, our estimates give us that

$$ \Sigma_{2}\ll_{\Delta,f}\frac{\varrho_{F}^{*}(\mathbf{k})\tau(k)}{\varphi(k)}\cdot D\cdot\left(1+\log\left(\frac{BL^{2}}{tk^{2}cb^{2}(n(-\Delta))^{2}D}\right)\right). $$

To bound $\Sigma_{1}$ , let us set up a few more facts. Then, we will split into the case when $F(x,y)$ has a linear factor and the case when it does not; this is equivalent to splitting into when $F(x,y)$ has a nontrivial solution over $\mathbb{Z}$ or not.

We first note that since $\Lambda(\alpha;ckd/g;b)\cap\Lambda(\mathbf{x}^{\prime};n(-\Delta))\subset\Lambda(\alpha;ckd/g;b)$ , we know that

$$ \lambda_{1}(\Lambda(\alpha;ckd/g;b)\cap\Lambda(\mathbf{x}^{\prime};n(-\Delta)))\geq\lambda_{1}(\Lambda(\alpha;ckd/g;b)). $$

Thus, we know that

$$ \Sigma_{1}\ll_{\Delta}\frac{B^{1/2}L}{(tk)^{1/2}}\sum_{d_{i}\sim D_{i}}\sum_{g\mid kcd}\frac{1}{g}\sum_{\alpha\in\mathcal{U}(\mathbf{c}\mathbf{k}\mathbf{d};b)}\frac{1}{\lambda_{1}(\Lambda(\alpha;ckd/g;b))}. $$

Next, since $\det(\Lambda(\alpha;ckd/g;b))=(ckd/g)b^{2}$ , we know that $\lambda_{1}\leq b\sqrt{kcd/g}.$ Further, if $\mathbf{v}$ is the shortest nontrivial vector in $\Lambda(\alpha;ckd/g;b)$ , then $\mathbf{v}$ satisfies that $\gcd(v_{1},v_{2})=b$ and that $k_{i}c_{i}d_{i}/g_{i}\mid F_{i}(\mathbf{v})$ for each $i$ (for some choice of decomposition of $g=g_{1}\dots g_{r})$ .

We now replace the summation over $\mathcal{U}(\mathbf{c}\mathbf{k}\mathbf{d};b)$ as $\mathbf{d}$ varies with summation over all possible shortest vectors of the lattice:

$$ \Sigma_{1}\ll_{\Delta}\frac{B^{1/2}L}{(tk)^{1/2}}\sum_{g\leq kcD}\frac{1}{g}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}|\mathbf{v}|\leq b\sqrt{kcD/g}\\
\gcd(v_{1},v_{2})=b\end{subarray}}\frac{1}{|\mathbf{v}|}\sum_{d_{i}\sim D_{i}}\prod_{i=1}^{r}\mathbf{1}_{k_{i}c_{i}d_{i}/g_{i}\mid F_{i}(\mathbf{v})}. $$

If $F(x,y)$ has no linear factors, i.e. no nontrivial solutions over $\mathbb{Z}$ , then we know that $F_{i}(\mathbf{v})\neq 0$ for each $i$ . However, if $F_{i}(x,y)$ is linear for some $i$ , then it is not impossible for $F_{i}(\mathbf{v})$ to be zero. Hence, this is the point at which we must split into analyzing the contributions differently in the two cases.

#### 9.2.1. $F(x,y)$ has no nontrivial solution over $\mathbb{Z}$

In this case, we can assume that $F_{i}(\mathbf{v})\neq 0$ for all $\mathbf{v}$ satisfying $\gcd(v_{1},v_{2})=b$ . Hence,

$$ \Sigma_{1}\ll_{\Delta}\frac{B^{1/2}L}{(tk)^{1/2}}\sum_{g\leq kcD}\frac{1}{g}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}|\mathbf{v}|\leq b\sqrt{kcD/g}\\
\gcd(v_{1},v_{2})=b\end{subarray}}\frac{1}{|\mathbf{v}|}\sum_{d_{i}\sim D_{i}/g_{i}}\prod_{i=1}^{r}\mathbf{1}_{k_{i}c_{i}d_{i}\mid F_{i}(\mathbf{v})}. $$

Recall that we use $\Delta$ to notate the Hooley $\Delta$ -function and that we use the convention that $\Delta(x)=0$ if $x\not\in\mathbb{Z}$ . Then we have the bound:

$$ \Sigma_{1}\ll_{\Delta}\frac{B^{1/2}L}{(tk)^{1/2}}\sum_{g\leq kcD}\frac{1}{g}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}|\mathbf{v}|\leq b\sqrt{kcD/g}\\
\gcd(v_{1},v_{2})=b\end{subarray}}\frac{1}{|\mathbf{v}|}\prod_{i=1}^{r}\Delta(F_{i}(\mathbf{v})/k_{i}c_{i}). $$

From Corollary 3.12, we can bound the sum over $\mathbf{v}$ by:

$$ \frac{\tau(b^{\deg(F)})}{b}\cdot\sqrt{kcD/g}\cdot\frac{(16\deg(F))^{\omega(ck)}}{ck}\prod_{i=1}^{r}\left(\sum_{s_{i}\ll\sqrt{kcD/g}}\frac{\varrho_{F_{i}}^{*}(s_{i})(\Delta(s_{i})-1)}{s_{i}^{2}}\right). $$

From Theorem 3.6, this is subsequently bounded by

$$ \frac{\tau(b^{\deg(F)})}{b}\cdot\frac{(16\deg(F))^{\omega(ck)}}{\sqrt{ck}}\cdot\sqrt{\frac{D}{g}}\cdot\exp(\gamma_{r}\sqrt{\log_{2}(kcD/g)\log_{3}(kcD/g)}), $$

where $\gamma_{r}>0$ is a constant depending on $r$ calculated explicitly in [31].

Recalling that $c$ is a constant only depending on $f$ , we know that

$$ \Sigma_{1}\ll_{\Delta,f}\frac{B^{1/2}L}{t^{1/2}}\cdot\frac{64^{\omega(k)}}{k}\cdot\frac{\tau(b^{4})}{b}\cdot\sqrt{D}\cdot\exp(\gamma_{r}\sqrt{\log_{2}(kcD)\log_{3}(kcD)})\sum_{g\leq kcD}\frac{1}{g^{3/2}}. $$

Thus, in the case when $F(x,y)$ has no nontrivial solutions over $\mathbb{Z}$ , we know that

$$ \Sigma_{1}\ll_{\Delta,f}\frac{B^{1/2}L}{t^{1/2}}\cdot\frac{64^{\omega(k)}}{k}\cdot\frac{\tau(b^{4})}{b}\cdot\sqrt{D}\cdot\exp(\gamma_{r}\sqrt{\log_{2}(kcD)\log_{3}(kcD)}). $$

#### 9.2.2. $F(x,y)$ has a nontrivial solution over $\mathbb{Z}$

We return to our expression of $\Sigma_{1}$ in (9.8) and split the sum over $\mathbf{v}$ by when $F_{i}(\mathbf{v})=0$ and otherwise:

$$ \Sigma_{1}\ll_{\Delta}\frac{B^{1/2}L}{(tk)^{1/2}}\sum_{g\leq kcD}\frac{1}{g}\left(\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}|\mathbf{v}|\leq b\sqrt{kcD/g}\\
\gcd(v_{1},v_{2})=b\\
F(\mathbf{v})\neq 0\end{subarray}}\frac{1}{|\mathbf{v}|}\sum_{d_{i}\sim D_{i}}\prod_{i=1}^{r}\mathbf{1}_{k_{i}c_{i}d_{i}/g_{i}\mid F_{i}(\mathbf{v})}+\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}|\mathbf{v}|\leq b\sqrt{kcD/g}\\
\gcd(v_{1},v_{2})=b\\
F(\mathbf{v})=0\end{subarray}}\frac{1}{|\mathbf{v}|}\sum_{d_{i}\sim D_{i}}\prod_{i=1}^{r}\mathbf{1}_{k_{i}c_{i}d_{i}/g_{i}\mid F_{i}(\mathbf{v})}\right). $$

By the argument above, we can see the sum over $F(\mathbf{v})\neq 0$ is bounded by

$$ \ll_{\Delta,f}\frac{B^{1/2}L}{t^{1/2}}\cdot\frac{64^{\omega(k)}}{k}\cdot\frac{\tau(b^{4})}{b}\cdot\sqrt{D}\cdot\exp(\gamma_{r}\sqrt{\log_{2}(kcD)\log_{3}(kcD)}). $$

So, it remains to handle the contribution when $F(\mathbf{v})=0$ – this implies that $F_{i}(\mathbf{v})=0$ for some linear factor $F_{i}\mid F$ .

Thus, we can bound the contribution when $F(\mathbf{v})=0$ by:

$$ \frac{B^{1/2}L}{(tk)^{1/2}}\sum_{g\leq kcD}\frac{1}{g}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}i=1\\
\deg(F_{i})=1\end{subarray}}^{r}\frac{D_{i}}{g_{i}}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}|\mathbf{v}|\leq b\sqrt{kcD/g}\\
\gcd(v_{1},v_{2})=b\\
F_{i}(\mathbf{v})=0\end{subarray}}\frac{1}{|\mathbf{v}|}. $$

For any linear factor $L(x,y)$ , we can compute that the sum:

$$ \sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}|\mathbf{v}|\leq b\sqrt{kcD/g}\\
L(\mathbf{v})=0\\
\gcd(v_{1},v_{2})=b\end{subarray}}\frac{1}{|\mathbf{v}|}\leq\frac{1}{b}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}|\mathbf{v}|\leq\sqrt{kcD/g}\\
L(\mathbf{v})=0\end{subarray}}\frac{1}{|\mathbf{v}|}\ll_{L}\frac{\log(kcD/g)}{b}. $$

Plugging the above estimate in, we have that the contribution from those $F(\mathbf{v})=0$ is bounded by:

$$ \frac{B^{1/2}L}{(tk)^{1/2}}\cdot\frac{1}{b}\cdot\max_{i:\deg(F_{i})=1}D_{i}\log(kcD)^{2}. $$

Thus, if $F(x,y)$ has a linear factor:

$$ \Sigma_{1}\ll_{\Delta,f}\frac{B^{1/2}L}{t^{1/2}}\cdot\frac{64^{\omega(k)}}{k}\cdot\frac{\tau(b^{4})}{b}\cdot\sqrt{D}\cdot\exp(\gamma_{r}\sqrt{\log_{2}(kcD)\log_{3}(kcD)})\\
+\frac{B^{1/2}L}{(tk)^{1/2}}\cdot\frac{1}{b}\cdot\max_{i:\deg(F_{i})=1}D_{i}\log(kcD)^{2}. $$

This completes the proof of Lemma 9.3

∎

### 9.3. From $\Lambda^{*}$ to $\Lambda$

We return to the sum that we actually want to evaluate:

$$ S(n,\mathbf{a},\mathbf{c},\mathbf{k},b;\mathbf{d})=\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}(x,y)\in(B/tk)^{1/2}\mathcal{B}(\mathbf{x}_{0},L)\\
b\mid x,y\\
k_{i}c_{i}d_{i}\mid F_{i}(x,y)\\
p_{-\Delta}(F(x,y)/c)=n\\
p_{\neg-\Delta}(F_{i}(x,y)/k_{i}c_{i})\equiv a_{i}\bmod-\Delta\end{subarray}}1. $$

In our notation above, this is given by

$$ \#(B/tk)^{1/2}\mathcal{B}(\mathbf{x}_{0},L)\cap\Lambda(\mathbf{c}\mathbf{k}\mathbf{d};b)\cap\Lambda(n,\mathbf{a}). $$

We now relate $\Lambda$ and $\Lambda^{*}$ : for any tuple $\mathbf{c}\mathbf{k}\mathbf{d}$ , we have that

$$ \Lambda(\mathbf{k}\mathbf{c}\mathbf{d};b)=\cup_{g_{i}\mid k_{i}c_{i}d_{i}}g\Lambda^{*}(c_{1}k_{1}d_{1}/g_{1}^{\dagger},\dots,c_{r}k_{r}d_{r}/g_{r}^{\dagger};b), $$

where $g=g_{1}\dots g_{r}$ and $g_{i}^{\dagger}=\gcd(g_{i}^{\deg(F_{i})},k_{i}c_{i}d_{i})$ . For notational simplicity, we write the vector above as $\mathbf{c}\mathbf{k}\mathbf{d}/\mathbf{g}^{\dagger}.$

Then we claim that

$$ \varrho_{F}(\mathbf{d};b,n,\mathbf{a},\mathbf{c},\mathbf{k})=\#\left\{\mathbf{x}\bmod bcdkn(-\Delta):\begin{array}[]{c}k_{i}c_{i}d_{i}\mid F_{i}(x,y),b\mid(x,y),\\
p_{-\Delta}(F(x,y))=n,p_{\neg-\Delta}(F_{i}(x,y)/k_{i}c_{i})\equiv a_{i}\bmod-\Delta\end{array}\right\}\\
=\sum_{g_{i}\mid k_{i}c_{i}d_{i}}\varrho_{F}^{*}(\mathbf{d}/\mathbf{g}^{\dagger};b,n,\mathbf{a},\mathbf{c},\mathbf{k})\cdot\left(\frac{g^{\dagger}}{g}\right)^{2}. $$

Indeed, by (9.10), the local count splits into a count of sums of the form:

$$ \#\left\{\mathbf{x}\bmod bcdkn(-\Delta):\begin{array}[]{c}k_{i}c_{i}d_{i}\mid F_{i}(x,y),b\mid(x,y),\gcd(x,y,kcd)=g\\
p_{-\Delta}(F(x,y))=n,p_{\neg-\Delta}(F_{i}(x,y)/k_{i}c_{i})\equiv a_{i}\bmod-\Delta\end{array}\right\}\\
=\#\left\{\mathbf{x}\bmod bcdkn(-\Delta)/g:\begin{array}[]{c}k_{i}c_{i}d_{i}\mid g^{\deg(F_{i})}F_{i}(x,y),b\mid(x,y),\gcd(x,y,kcd/g)=1\\
p_{-\Delta}(F(x,y))=n,p_{\neg-\Delta}(F_{i}(x,y)/k_{i}c_{i})\equiv a_{i}\bmod-\Delta\end{array}\right\}\\
=\left(\frac{g^{\dagger}}{g}\right)^{2}\cdot\#\left\{\mathbf{x}\bmod bcdkn(-\Delta)/g^{\dagger}:\begin{array}[]{c}k_{i}c_{i}d_{i}/g_{i}^{\dagger}\mid F_{i}(x,y),b\mid(x,y),\gcd(x,y,kcd/g^{\dagger})=1\\
p_{-\Delta}(F(x,y))=n,p_{\neg-\Delta}(F_{i}(x,y)/k_{i}c_{i})\equiv a_{i}\bmod-\Delta\end{array}\right\}. $$

This completes the claim.

Let us define a modification of (9.5):

$$ S^{*}_{g}(n,\mathbf{a},\mathbf{c},\mathbf{k},b;\mathbf{d}):=\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}(x,y)\in\frac{1}{g}(B/tk)^{1/2}\mathcal{B}(\mathbf{x}_{0},L)\\
b\mid x,y\\
k_{i}c_{i}d_{i}\mid F_{i}(x,y)\\
p_{-\Delta}(F(x,y)/c)=n\\
p_{\neg-\Delta}(F_{i}(x,y)/k_{i}c_{i})\equiv a_{i}\bmod-\Delta\end{subarray}}\mathbf{1}_{\gcd(x,y,kcd)=1}. $$

Consequently,

$$ E(\mathbf{D})\ll\sum_{d_{i}\sim D_{i}}\sum_{g_{i}\mid k_{i}c_{i}d_{i}}\left|S^{*}_{g}(n,\mathbf{a},\mathbf{c},\mathbf{k},b;\mathbf{d}/\mathbf{g}^{\dagger})-\frac{\varrho_{F}^{*}(\mathbf{d}/\mathbf{g}^{\dagger};b,\mathbf{a},\mathbf{c},\mathbf{k})}{(cdbn(-\Delta))^{2}}\cdot\frac{BL^{2}}{tk^{3}}\cdot\left(\frac{g^{\dagger}}{g}\right)^{2}\right|. $$

Reordering the summation and noting that there are $\leq\tau(g_{i}^{\deg(F_{i})})$ possible values of $d_{i}$ that achieve the same value of $k_{i}c_{i}d_{i}/g_{i}$ , we have:

$$ E(\mathbf{D})\ll\sum_{g_{i}\leq k_{i}c_{i}D_{i}}\tau(g_{i}^{\deg(F_{i})})\sum_{d_{i}\sim D_{i}/g_{i}}\left|S^{*}_{g}(n,\mathbf{a},\mathbf{c},\mathbf{k},b;\mathbf{d})-\frac{\varrho_{F}^{*}(\mathbf{d};b,\mathbf{a},\mathbf{c},\mathbf{k})}{(cdbn(-\Delta))^{2}}\cdot\frac{BL^{2}}{tk^{3}}\cdot\frac{1}{g^{2}}\right|. $$

Let us split the above summation into two ranges by the value

$$ G=1+\frac{BL^{2}}{tkD} $$

and write

$$ E_{\geq G}(\mathbf{D})=\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}g_{i}\leq k_{i}c_{i}D_{i}\\
g\geq G\end{subarray}}\tau(g_{i}^{\deg(F_{i})})\sum_{d_{i}\sim D_{i}/g_{i}}\left|S^{*}_{g}(n,\mathbf{a},\mathbf{c},\mathbf{k},b;\mathbf{d})-\frac{\varrho_{F}^{*}(\mathbf{d};b,\mathbf{a},\mathbf{c},\mathbf{k})}{(cdbn(-\Delta))^{2}}\cdot\frac{BL^{2}}{tk^{3}}\cdot\frac{1}{g^{2}}\right|, $$

$$ E_{\leq G}(\mathbf{D})=\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}g_{i}\leq k_{i}c_{i}D_{i}\\
g\leq G\end{subarray}}\tau(g_{i}^{\deg(F_{i})})\sum_{d_{i}\sim D_{i}/g_{i}}\left|S^{*}_{g}(n,\mathbf{a},\mathbf{c},\mathbf{k},b;\mathbf{d})-\frac{\varrho_{F}^{*}(\mathbf{d};b,\mathbf{a},\mathbf{c},\mathbf{k})}{(cdbn(-\Delta))^{2}}\cdot\frac{BL^{2}}{tk^{3}}\cdot\frac{1}{g^{2}}\right|. $$

First, let us bound $E_{\geq G}(\mathbf{D}).$ For any fixed tuple $\mathbf{g}$ , we claim that the following bound holds by Corollary 3.12:

$$ \sum_{d_{i}\sim D_{i}/g_{i}}\left|S^{*}_{g}(n,\mathbf{a},\mathbf{c},\mathbf{k},b;\mathbf{d})-\frac{\varrho_{F}^{*}(\mathbf{d};b,\mathbf{a},\mathbf{c},\mathbf{k})}{(cdbn(-\Delta))^{2}}\cdot\frac{BL^{2}}{tk^{3}}\cdot\frac{1}{g^{2}}\right|\\
\ll_{\Delta}\sum_{d_{i}\sim D_{i}/g_{i}}S^{*}_{g}(n,\mathbf{a},\mathbf{c},\mathbf{k},b;\mathbf{d})+\sum_{d_{i}\sim D_{i}/g_{i}}\frac{\varrho_{F}^{*}(\mathbf{d};b,\mathbf{a},\mathbf{c},\mathbf{k})}{(cdbn(-\Delta))^{2}}\cdot\frac{BL^{2}}{tk^{3}}\cdot\frac{1}{g^{2}}\\
\ll_{\Delta,f}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}(x,y)\in\frac{1}{g}(B/tk)^{1/2}\mathcal{B}(\mathbf{x}_{0},L)\\
b\mid x,y\end{subarray}}\prod_{i=1}^{r}\Delta(F_{i}(x,y)/k_{i}c_{i})+\frac{1}{g^{2}}\cdot\frac{BL^{2}}{t}\cdot\frac{\varrho_{F}^{*}(\mathbf{k})}{k^{3}}\cdot\left(\log(2D/g)-\log(D/g)+1\right)^{r}\\
\ll_{\Delta,f}\frac{BL^{2}}{tkb^{2}g^{2}}\cdot\frac{64^{\omega(k)}}{k}\cdot\exp(\gamma_{r}\sqrt{\log_{2}(B/tk)\log_{3}(B/tk)})+\frac{1}{g^{2}}\cdot\frac{BL^{2}}{t}\cdot\frac{\varrho_{F}^{*}(\mathbf{k})}{k^{3}}. $$

Thus, we have that

$$ E_{\geq G}(\mathbf{D})\ll_{\Delta,f}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}g_{i}\leq k_{i}c_{i}D_{i}\\
g\geq G\end{subarray}}\frac{\tau(g_{i}^{\deg(F_{i})})}{g^{2}}\cdot\left(\frac{BL^{2}}{tkb^{2}}\cdot\frac{64^{\omega(k)}}{k}\cdot\exp(\gamma_{r}\sqrt{\log_{2}(B/tk)\log_{3}(B/tk)})+\frac{BL^{2}}{t}\cdot\frac{\varrho_{F}^{*}(\mathbf{k})}{k^{3}}\right)\\
\ll_{\Delta,f}\left(\frac{BL^{2}}{tkb^{2}}\cdot\frac{64^{\omega(k)}}{k}\cdot\exp(\gamma_{r}\sqrt{\log_{2}(B/tk)\log_{3}(B/tk)})+\frac{BL^{2}}{t}\cdot\frac{\varrho_{F}^{*}(\mathbf{k})}{k^{3}}\right)\cdot\frac{\log(G)^{8}}{G}. $$

By our choice of $G$ , we can bound $E_{\geq G}(\mathbf{D})$ by:

$$ \log\left(1+\frac{BL^{2}}{tkD}\right)^{8}\left(\frac{D}{b^{2}}\cdot\frac{64^{\omega(k)}}{k}\cdot\exp(\gamma_{r}\sqrt{\log_{2}(B/tk)\log_{3}(B/tk)})+D\cdot\frac{\varrho_{F}^{*}(\mathbf{k})}{k^{2}}\right). $$

For $E_{\leq G}(\mathbf{D})$ , we now apply Lemma 9.3 to this inner sum, with our region changed to $\frac{1}{g}(B/tk)^{1/2}\mathcal{B}(\mathbf{x}_{0},L)$ . If $F(x,y)$ has no linear factors, then

$$ E_{\leq G}(\mathbf{D})\ll_{\Delta,f}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}g_{i}\leq k_{i}c_{i}D_{i}\\
g\leq G\end{subarray}}\tau(g_{i}^{\deg(F_{i})})\frac{\varrho_{F}^{*}(\mathbf{k})\tau(k)}{\varphi(k)}\cdot\frac{D}{g}\cdot\log(G)\\
+\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}g_{i}\leq k_{i}c_{i}D_{i}\\
g\leq G\end{subarray}}\frac{B^{1/2}L}{gt^{1/2}}\cdot\frac{64^{\omega(k)}}{k}\cdot\frac{\tau(b^{4})}{b}\cdot\sqrt{\frac{D}{g}}\cdot\exp(\gamma_{r}\sqrt{\log_{2}(kcD)\log_{3}(kcD)}). $$

Evaluating these summands, we see that

$$ E_{\leq G}(\mathbf{D})\ll_{\Delta,f}\frac{\varrho_{F}^{*}(\mathbf{k})\tau(k)}{\varphi(k)}\cdot D\cdot\log\left(1+\frac{BL^{2}}{tkD}\right)^{9}\\
+\frac{B^{1/2}L}{t^{1/2}}\cdot\frac{64^{\omega(k)}}{k}\cdot\frac{\tau(b^{4})}{b}\cdot\sqrt{D}\cdot\exp(\gamma_{r}\sqrt{\log_{2}(kcD)\log_{3}(kcD)}). $$

Now, if $F(x,y)$ has a linear factor, then there is an extra term:

$$ \sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}g_{i}\leq k_{i}c_{i}D_{i}\\
g\leq G\end{subarray}}\tau(g_{i}^{\deg(F_{i})})\cdot\frac{B^{1/2}L}{g(tk)^{1/2}}\cdot\frac{1}{b}\cdot\max_{i:\deg(F_{i})=1}\frac{D_{i}}{g_{i}}\log(kcD)^{2}\\
\ll_{\Delta,f}\frac{B^{1/2}L}{(tk)^{1/2}}\cdot\frac{1}{b}\cdot\max_{i:\deg(F_{i})=1}D_{i}\log(kcD)^{2}\log\left(1+\frac{BL^{2}}{tkD}\right)^{8}. $$

Combining this bound with (9.12) and (9.13) gives Proposition 9.1.

## 10. Large moduli and Hooley’s $\Delta$ -function

In this section, we will discuss how to handle the sum for larger $\mathbf{d}$ : let us write

$$ T(n,\mathbf{a},\mathbf{c},\mathbf{k},b;\mathbf{D}):=\sum_{d_{i}\sim D_{i}}\chi(d)S(n,\mathbf{a},\mathbf{c},\mathbf{k},b;\mathbf{d}), $$

where $S(n,\mathbf{a},\mathbf{c},\mathbf{k},b;\mathbf{d})$ is defined in (8.7). If $F(x,y)$ has a linear factor $F_{1}(x,y)$ , let us define

$$ T_{L}(n,\mathbf{a},\mathbf{c},\mathbf{k},b;D_{1}):=\sum_{d_{1}\sim D_{1}}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}d_{i}\ll(B/tk)^{\deg(F_{i})/4}(n_{i}k_{i})^{-1/2}\end{subarray}}\chi(d)S(n,\mathbf{a},\mathbf{c},\mathbf{k},b;\mathbf{d}). $$

We will provide an upper bound for these sums. This proof is based off of de la Bretèche and Tenenbaum’s [25] and Heath Brown’s [33] (for $F(x,y)$ with linear factors) treatment of the large moduli terms.

#### Proposition 10.1.

Let $F$ be a squarefree binary form. Let $\mathbf{D}=(D_{i})_{i=1}^{r}$ satisfy that $\log(D)\gg\log(B/kt)$ . Then the following bound holds:

$$ T(n,\mathbf{a},\mathbf{c},\mathbf{k},b;\mathbf{D})\ll\left(\frac{B}{b^{2}tk^{2}}+\frac{B^{3/4}\nu_{1}(k)^{1/2}}{bt^{3/4}k^{5/4}}\right)\cdot(4\deg(F))^{\omega(k)}\\
\times\log(B/tk)^{\rho_{\Delta,f}/2-1-10^{-5}}\cdot\left(\frac{B}{tkD}+\frac{tkD}{B}+\log\log(B/tk)\right)^{1/2}. $$

#### Proposition 10.2.

Let $F$ be a squarefree binary form with a linear factor $F_{1}(x,y)$ . Then, the following bound holds:

$$ T(n,\mathbf{a},\mathbf{c},\mathbf{k},b;D_{1})\ll\frac{B(16\deg(F))^{\omega(k)}}{tk^{2}}\cdot\log(B/tk)^{\rho_{\Delta,f}-2-10^{-5}}. $$

### 10.1. Relation to the twisted Hooley’s $\Delta$ -function

We first observe that

$$ T(n,\mathbf{a},\mathbf{c},\mathbf{k},b;\mathbf{D})\leq\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}(x,y)\in(B/tk)^{1/2}\mathcal{B}(\mathbf{x}_{0},L)\\
b\mid x,y\\
\exists d_{i}\sim D_{i}:k_{i}c_{i}d_{i}\mid F_{i}(x,y)\\
p_{-\Delta}(F(x,y)/c)=n\\
p_{\neg-\Delta}(F_{i}(x,y)/k_{i}c_{i}d_{i})\equiv a_{i}\bmod-\Delta\end{subarray}}\prod_{i=1}^{r}\Delta(F_{i}(x,y)/k_{i}c_{i},\chi). $$

Since $\Delta(n,\chi)\geq 0$ , we can remove a few conditions and ask to bound:

$$ \sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}|x|,|y|\leq(B/tk)^{1/2}\\
b\mid x,y\\
\exists d_{i}\sim D_{i}:k_{i}c_{i}d_{i}\mid F_{i}(x,y)\end{subarray}}\prod_{i=1}^{r}\Delta(F_{i}(x,y)/k_{i}c_{i},\chi). $$

After applying Cauchy-Schwarz, we achieve the upper bound of

$$ T(n,\mathbf{a},\mathbf{c},\mathbf{k},b;\mathbf{D})\leq\left(\#\{|x|,|y|\leq(B/tk)^{1/2}:b\mid(x,y),\exists d_{i}\sim D_{i},k_{i}c_{i}d_{i}\mid F_{i}(x,y)\}\right)^{1/2}\\
\times\left(\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}|x|,|y|\leq(B/tk)^{1/2}\\
b\mid x,y\end{subarray}}\prod_{i=1}^{r}\Delta(F_{i}(x,y)/k_{i}c_{i},\chi)^{2}\right)^{1/2}. $$

Let us apply Lemma 3.14 to the first quantity:

$$ \#\{|x|,|y|\leq(B/tk)^{1/2}:b\mid(x,y),\exists d_{i}\sim D_{i},k_{i}c_{i}d_{i}\mid F_{i}(x,y)\}\\
\leq\#\{|x|,|y|\leq(B/tk)^{1/2}:b\mid(x,y),k\mid F(x,y),\exists d\sim D,d\mid F(x,y)\}\\
\ll\left(\frac{\deg(F)^{\omega(k)}}{b^{2}k}\cdot\frac{B}{tk}+\nu_{1}(k)\left(\frac{B}{tk}\right)^{1/2}\right)\cdot\left(\frac{B}{tkD}+\frac{tkD}{B}+\log\log(B/tk)\right)\log(B/tk)^{-10^{-4}}. $$

Here $\nu_{1}(k)=\sum_{\alpha\in\mathcal{U}(k)}\lambda_{1}(\Lambda(\alpha;k))^{-1}$ . We note that tracking through the proof of equation (7.41) in [25], one can add the lattice constraints that $b\mid x,y$ and achieve the upper bound mentioned with an additional factor of $b^{-2}$ (recall that $b\leq\log(B)^{10^{-7}}$ is much smaller that $B/tk\geq\exp(\sqrt{\log(B)})$ ). Similarly, after tracking through the proof of (7.41) in [25] with the lattice condition that $k\mid F(x,y)$ , we achieve the bound above; in §9, it was seen that this condition gives $\deg(F)^{\omega(k)}$ such lattices of determinant $k$ .

Next, we apply Corollary 3.12 to the second sum:

$$ \sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}|x|,|y|\leq(B/tk)^{1/2}\\
b\mid x,y\end{subarray}}\prod_{i=1}^{r}\Delta(F_{i}(x,y)/k_{i}c_{i},\chi)^{2}\ll\frac{B}{tk\log(B/tk)}\cdot\frac{(16\deg(F))^{\omega(k)}}{b^{2}k}\prod_{i=1}^{r}\left(\sum_{s_{i}\ll B/tk}\Delta(s_{i},\chi)^{2}\frac{\varrho_{F_{i}}(s_{i})}{s_{i}^{2}}\right). $$

Here we have again restricted to the lattice defined by $b\mid(x,y)$ . If $F_{i}(x,y)$ is irreducible over the quadratic field $K$ , then by Theorem 3.9, we have that

$$ \sum_{s_{i}\ll B/tk}\Delta(s_{i},\chi)^{2}\cdot\frac{\varrho_{F_{i}}(s_{i})}{s_{i}^{2}}\ll\sum_{s_{i}\ll B/tk}\Delta(s_{i},\chi)^{2}\cdot\frac{\varrho_{f_{i}}(s_{i})}{s_{i}}\ll\exp(C\sqrt{\log_{2}(B)\log_{3}(B)}), $$

for an explicit $C>0$ . Otherwise, we use a trivial bound:

$$ \sum_{s_{i}\ll B/tk}\Delta(s_{i},\chi)^{2}\cdot\frac{\varrho_{F_{i}}(s_{i})}{s_{i}^{2}}\ll\sum_{s_{i}\ll B/tk}\Delta(s_{i})^{2}\cdot\frac{\varrho_{F_{i}}(s_{i})}{s_{i}^{2}}\ll\log(B/tk)\exp(C\sqrt{\log_{2}(B)\log_{3}(B)}). $$

Here we have used the results of de la Bretèche and Tenenbaum in [26, Theorem 1.1] for averages of higher powers of $\Delta(n)$ correlated with local counts of polynomials.

Combining these two bounds, we have that

$$ T(n,\mathbf{a},\mathbf{c},\mathbf{k},b;\mathbf{D})\leq\left(\frac{B}{b^{2}tk^{2}}+\frac{B^{3/4}\nu_{1}(k)^{1/2}}{bt^{3/4}k^{5/4}}\right)\cdot(4\deg(F))^{\omega(k)}\cdot\left(\frac{B}{tkD}+\frac{tkD}{B}+\log\log(B/tk)\right)^{1/2}\\
\times\exp(C^{\prime}\sqrt{\log_{2}(B)\log_{3}(B)})\cdot\log(B/tk)^{\rho_{\Delta,f}/2-1-10^{-4}}. $$

This completes the proof of Proposition 10.1.∎

### 10.2. Linear factors

Let us assume that $F(x,y)$ has a linear factor that we denote as $F_{1}(x,y)=L(x,y)$ . Again, we enlarge our region and remove the short box constraints, since the terms being summed are non-negative. In this case, we have that

$$ T(n,\mathbf{a},\mathbf{c},\mathbf{k},b;D_{1})\leq\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}|x|,|y|\leq(B/tk)^{1/2}\\
b\mid x,y\end{subarray}}\Delta(L(x,y)/k_{1}r_{1}c_{1},\chi;D_{1})\prod_{i=2}^{r}(1\star\chi)(F_{i}(x,y)/k_{i}c_{i},\chi), $$

where we define the localized twisted Hooley $\Delta$ function as

$$ \Delta(n,\chi;D):=\left|\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}d\mid n\\
d\sim D\end{subarray}}\chi(d)\right|. $$

Next, we separate the sum by certain values of $L(x,y)$ :

$$ T(n,\mathbf{a},\mathbf{c},\mathbf{k},b;D_{1})\leq\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}m\ll(B/tk)^{1/2}/k_{1}r_{1}c_{1}\\
b\mid m\\
\exists d_{1}\sim D_{1},d_{1}\mid m\end{subarray}}\Delta(m,\chi;D_{1})\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}|x|,|y|\leq(B/tk)^{1/2}\\
b\mid x,y\\
L(x,y)=mk_{1}r_{1}c_{1}\end{subarray}}\prod_{i=2}^{r}(1\star\chi)(F_{i}(x,y)/k_{i}c_{i},\chi). $$

For now let us fix a $m$ . The restriction $L(x,y)=mk_{1}r_{1}c_{1}$ allows us to rewrite the polynomial $F_{i}(x,y)$ as a single variable polynomial $F_{i,m}(x).$ In particular, we have that

$$ \sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}|x|,|y|\leq(B/tk)^{1/2}\\
b\mid x,y\\
L(x,y)=mk_{1}c_{1}\end{subarray}}\prod_{i=2}^{r}(1\star\chi)(F_{i}(x,y)/k_{i}c_{i},\chi)\ll\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}x\ll(B/tk)^{1/2}\\
b\mid x\end{subarray}}\prod_{i=2}^{r}(1\star\chi)(F_{i,m}(x)/k_{i}c_{i},\chi). $$

So, we apply Corollary 3.12 to the sum above:

$$ \ll\frac{B^{1/2}}{b(tk)^{1/2}}\cdot\frac{(16\deg(F))^{\omega(k)}}{k}\prod_{i=1}^{r}\exp\left(\sum_{p_{i}\ll B/tk}\frac{\varrho_{F_{i,m}}(p_{i})\chi(p_{i})}{p_{i}}\right). $$

Now, we can see that if $\varrho_{F_{i}}^{\prime}(p)$ is the original number of roots of $F_{i}(x,1)\bmod p$ , then for $p$ not dividing $m$ , we have that

$$ \varrho_{F_{i},m}(p)=\varrho_{F_{i}}(p). $$

So, we write the above sum as

$$ \sum_{i=2}^{r}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}p_{i}\ll X\\
p_{i}\nmid m\end{subarray}}\frac{\varrho_{F_{i}}^{\prime}(p_{i})\chi(p_{i})}{p_{i}}+\sum_{i=2}^{r}\sum_{p_{i}\mid m}\frac{\varrho_{F_{i,m}}(p_{i})\chi(p_{i})}{p_{i}}. $$

We consider

$$ \exp\left(\sum_{i=2}^{r}\sum_{p\mid m}\frac{\varrho_{F_{i,m}}(p_{i})\chi(p_{i})}{p_{i}}-\sum_{p_{i}\mid m}\frac{\varrho_{F_{i}}^{\prime}(p_{i})\chi(p_{i})}{p_{i}}\right)\ll\prod_{i=2}^{r}\prod_{p_{i}\mid m}\left(\frac{1-\varrho_{F_{i,m}}(p_{i})/p_{i}}{1-\varrho_{F_{i}}^{\prime}(p_{i})/p_{i}}\right)\ll\prod_{i=2}^{r}\left(\frac{\sigma(m)}{m}\right)^{\deg(F_{i})}, $$

where we use the notation $\sigma(m)=\sum_{d\mid m}d.$ Here, we have used [33, (4.6)]. Now since $m\ll B/tk$ , the above is bounded by

$$ \ll\prod_{i=2}^{r}\log\log(B/tk)^{\deg(F_{i})}\ll\log\log(B/tk)^{\deg(F)-1}. $$

In summary, we have that

$$ \sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}x\ll(B/tk)^{1/2}\\
b\mid x\end{subarray}}\prod_{i=2}^{r}(1\star\chi)(F_{i,m}(x)/k_{i}c_{i},\chi)\ll\frac{B^{1/2}\log\log(B/tk)^{\deg(F)-1}}{b(tk)^{1/2}}\cdot\frac{(8\deg(F))^{\omega(k)}}{k}\\
\times\exp\left(\sum_{i=2}^{r}\sum_{p_{i}\ll B/tk}\frac{\varrho_{F_{i}}^{\prime}(p_{i})\chi(p_{i})}{p_{i}}\right). $$

Since $L(x,y)$ was a linear factor of $F(x,y)$ , we know that the Picard rank satisfies

$$ \rho_{\Delta,F}=\rho_{\Delta,F_{2}...F_{r}}. $$

Thus, we get that

$$ \sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}x\ll(B/tk)^{1/2}\\
b\mid x\end{subarray}}\prod_{i=2}^{r}(1\star\chi)(F_{i,m}(x)/k_{i}c_{i},\chi)\ll\frac{B^{1/2}\log(B/tk)^{\rho_{\Delta,F}-2}\log\log(B/tk)^{\deg(F)-1}}{b(tk)^{1/2}}\cdot\frac{(16\deg(F))^{\omega(k)}}{k}. $$

Here we have again used Corollary 3.16 that the order of the pole of $\xi(s;F,\chi)$ is given by $\rho_{\Delta,f}-2.$

Applying the above bound to the inner sum of (10.1), we see that

$$ T(n,\mathbf{a},\mathbf{c},\mathbf{k},b;D_{1})\leq\frac{B^{1/2}\log(B/tk)^{\rho_{\Delta,f}-2}\log\log(B/tk)^{\deg(F)-1}}{b(tk)^{1/2}}\cdot\frac{(16\deg(F))^{\omega(k)}}{k}\\
\times\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}m\ll(B/tk)^{1/2}/k_{1}c_{1}\\
b\mid m\\
\exists d_{1}\sim D_{1},d_{1}\mid m\end{subarray}}\Delta(m,\chi;D_{1}). $$

Applying the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality to the second sum, this final sum is bounded by:

$$ \ll\#\{m\ll(B/tk)^{1/2}/k_{1}c_{1}:b\mid m,\exists d_{1}\sim D_{1},d_{1}\mid m\}^{1/2}\times\left(\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}m\ll(B/tk)^{1/2}/k_{1}c_{1}\\
b\mid m\end{subarray}}\Delta(m,\chi)^{2}\right)^{1/2}. $$

Now we apply Lemma 3.13 to the first sum, and Theorem 3.10 and Theorem 3.9 to the second to get the upper bound:

$$ T(n,\mathbf{a},\mathbf{c},\mathbf{k},b;D_{1})\leq\frac{B\log(B/t)^{\rho_{\Delta,f}-2-10^{-5}}}{tk}\cdot\frac{(16\deg(F))^{\omega(k)}}{k}. $$

This completes the proof of Proposition 10.2.

## 11. The asymptotics

In this section, we will finally prove Proposition 8.1 and establish the asymptotic in Proposition 5.11. To do so, we bring in ingredients from the preceding sections. Unfortunately, it is in this section where we are confronted with a notationally-challenging problem – while morally equivalent, the proofs for various factorizations of $F(x,y)$ must be treated slightly differently. As such, we have to do casework on the factorization-type of $F(x,y)$ in §11.1.

We also highlight that the calculations in §11.2 are the jumping-off point for computing the leading constant in §12. In particular, the notation that is used in §12 is established in this section.

### 11.1. Proof of Proposition 8.1

Let us first recall the statement of Proposition 8.1:

#### Proposition.

Let $F(x,y)$ be a squarefree binary form of degree $\leq 4$ and $L\gg\log(B)^{-10^{-10}}.$ Then we have that for $t$ and $k$ satisfying $tk\leq B/\exp(\sqrt{\log(B)}),$ the following holds:

$$ S(X_{\Delta,f},\mathcal{B}(\mathbf{x}_{0},L);q_{1},q_{2},t,k)=\frac{BL^{2}}{tk^{3}}\cdot C_{q_{1},q_{2},f,k}(B/tk)\cdot\left(1+O\left(\log(B)^{-10^{-7}}\right)\right)\\
+O\left(\frac{64^{\omega(k)}\log(k)B}{tk^{3/2}}\cdot\log(B)^{\rho_{\Delta,f}-2-10^{-7}}+\frac{B^{3/4}}{(tk)^{3/4}}\cdot\left(L+(4\deg(F))^{\omega(k)}\nu_{1}(k)^{1/2}\right)\cdot\log(B)^{-10^{-7}}\right), $$

where $C_{q_{1},q_{2},f,k}(B/tk)$ is an expression that depends on the factorization of $F(x,y)$ . Additionally, for a fixed value of $k$ , there exists a constant $c_{q_{1},q_{2},f,k}$ such that

$$ C_{q_{1},q_{2},f,k}(B/tk)=c_{q_{1},q_{2},f,k}\log(B/tk)^{\rho_{\Delta,f}-2}. $$

#### Remark 11.1.

Note that since $tk\leq B/\exp(\sqrt{\log(B)}),$ we have that $\log(B)\ll\log(B/tk)\ll\log(B).$ We use these interchangeably in this section when referring to error terms.

Before delving into the case work for this proof, let us outline the general strategy. After applying the reductions discussed in §8, the sum that we wish to analyze takes the form:

$$ S(X_{\Delta,f},\mathcal{B}(\mathbf{x}_{0},L);q_{1},q_{2},t,k)\\
\sim\sum_{c_{ij}\mid\textrm{Res}(F_{i},F_{j})}\mu(c)\chi(c)\sum_{b\leq\log(B)^{10^{-7}}}\mu(b)\cdot\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}n\leq\log(B)^{10^{-7}}\\
p\mid n\implies p\mid-\Delta\end{subarray}}\chi_{q_{1}}(p_{q_{2}}(n))\chi_{q_{2}}(p_{q_{1}}(n))\mathbf{1}_{\exists\mathfrak{a}:N(\mathfrak{a})=n}\\
\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}\mathbf{a}\bmod-\Delta\\
\gcd(a_{i},-\Delta)=1\end{subarray}}\prod_{i=1}^{r}\chi_{q_{1}}(a_{i})(1+\chi(a_{i}))\sum_{d_{i}\ll(B/tk)^{\deg(F_{i})/2}}\prod_{i=1}^{r}\chi(d_{i})S(n,\mathbf{a},\mathbf{c},\mathbf{k},b;\mathbf{d}). $$

We proceed by splitting up the sum over $d_{i}$ into sums over “small” and “large” moduli – either $d\leq(B/tk)^{\deg(F)/4}\log(B)^{-\epsilon}$ or $d\geq(B/tk)^{\deg(F)/4}\log(B)^{-\epsilon}$ . We remark that if $F(x,y)$ has linear factors, the cutoff point for being considered a “small” or “large” modulus is shifted by $\log(B)$ .

For “small” moduli, our level of distribution result (Proposition 9.1) enables us to achieve the main term:

$$ \frac{BL^{2}}{tk^{3}}\cdot\sum_{c_{ij}\mid\textrm{Res}(F_{i},F_{j})}\frac{\mu(c)\chi(c)}{c}\sum_{b\leq\log(B)^{10^{-7}}}\frac{\mu(b)}{b^{2}}\cdot\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}n\leq\log(B)^{10^{-7}}\\
p\mid n\implies p\mid-\Delta\end{subarray}}\frac{\chi_{q_{1}}(p_{q_{2}}(n))\chi_{q_{2}}(p_{q_{1}}(n))\mathbf{1}_{\exists\mathfrak{a}:N(\mathfrak{a})=n}}{n^{2}}\\
\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}\mathbf{a}\bmod-\Delta\\
\gcd(a_{i},-\Delta)=1\end{subarray}}\frac{\prod_{i=1}^{r}\chi_{q_{1}}(a_{i})(1+\chi(a_{i}))}{(-\Delta)^{2}}\sum_{d_{i}\ll(B/tk)^{\deg(F_{i})/2}(\log B)^{-\epsilon}}\prod_{i=1}^{r}\chi(d_{i})\frac{\varrho_{F}(\mathbf{d};b,n,\mathbf{a},\mathbf{c},\mathbf{k})}{d^{2}}. $$

For “large” moduli, the analysis on the twisted Hooley $\Delta$ -function (Propostion 10.1 or Proposition 10.2) gives us that these terms contribute negligibly. For these terms, we establish a bound of the form:

$$ \sum_{d\geq(B/tk)^{\deg(F)/2}\log(B)^{-\epsilon}}\chi(d)S(n,\mathbf{a},\mathbf{c},\mathbf{k},b;\mathbf{d})\ll\log(B)^{\rho_{\Delta,f}-2-10^{-5}}\cdot\left(\frac{B}{b^{2}tk^{2}}+\frac{B^{3/4}\nu_{1}(k)^{1/2}}{(tk)^{3/4}}\right). $$

Note that since $b,n\leq\log(B)^{10^{-7}}$ compared to our saving of $\log(B)^{-10^{-5}},$ we will get a sufficient error term here.

After careful analysis, we can rewrite this main term as

$$ \frac{BL^{2}}{tk^{2}}\cdot\cdot\sum_{c_{ij}\mid\textrm{Res}(F_{i},F_{j})}\mu(c)\chi(c)\cdot\bigtriangledown_{q_{1},q_{2}}(\mathbf{c})\cdot V(\mathbf{c};B/tk), $$

where $\bigtriangledown_{q_{1},q_{2}}(\mathbf{c})$ is a constant that detects local obstructions at primes $p\mid-\Delta$ for $X^{*}_{\Delta,f_{1},...,f_{r},\mathbf{c}}$ (formally defined in (Definition 11.3)) and $V(\mathbf{c};B/tk)$ is a sum related to the Dirichlet series $\xi(s;F,\chi)$ (defined in (3.2)). We determine that $V(\mathbf{c};B/tk)$ satisfies that

$$ V(\mathbf{c};B/tk)\sim c_{q_{1},q_{2},f,k,\mathbf{c}}\log(B/tk)^{\rho_{\Delta,f}-2}. $$

Additionally, in §12, we will analyse the constant $c_{q_{1},q_{2},f,k,\mathbf{c}}$ further.

Now, we proceed with the full proof of Proposition 8.1. We start with the case work on the factorizaton of $F(x,y)$ .

#### 11.1.1. $F(x,y)$ is irreducible

Since $F(x,y)$ is irreducible, we can skip the reductions in §8.1. Applying the reductions of §8.2, §8.3, and §8.4, we achieve:

$$ \displaystyle S(X_{\Delta,f},\mathcal{B}(\mathbf{x}_{0},L);q_{1},q_{2},t,k) \displaystyle=\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}n\ll\log(B)^{10^{-7}}\\
p\mid n\implies p\mid-\Delta\end{subarray}}\chi_{q_{1}}(p_{q_{2}}(n))\chi_{q_{2}}(p_{q_{1}}(n))\mathbf{1}_{\exists\mathfrak{a}:N(\mathfrak{a})=n}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}a\bmod-\Delta\\
\gcd(a,-\Delta)=1\end{subarray}}\chi_{q_{1}}(a)S(n,a,1,k) \displaystyle\hskip 142.26378pt+O\left(\frac{BL^{2}}{tk^{2}}\cdot\log(B)^{\rho_{\Delta,f}-2-10^{-7}}\right) \displaystyle=\sum_{b\leq\log(B)^{10^{-7}}}\mu(b)\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}n\ll\log(B)^{10^{-7}}\\
p\mid n\implies p\mid-\Delta\end{subarray}}\chi_{q_{1}}(p_{q_{2}}(n))\chi_{q_{2}}(p_{q_{1}}(n))\mathbf{1}_{\exists\mathfrak{a}:N(\mathfrak{a})=n}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}a\bmod-\Delta\\
\gcd(a,-\Delta)=1\end{subarray}}\chi_{q_{1}}(a)S(n,a,1,k;b) \displaystyle\hskip 142.26378pt+O\left(\frac{BL^{2}}{tk^{2}}\log(B)^{\rho_{\Delta,f}-2-10^{-7}}\right) \displaystyle=\sum_{b\leq\log(B)^{10^{-7}}}\mu(b)\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}n\ll\log(B)^{10^{-7}}\\
p\mid n\implies p\mid-\Delta\end{subarray}}\chi_{q_{1}}(p_{q_{2}}(n))\chi_{q_{2}}(p_{q_{1}}(n))\mathbf{1}_{\exists\mathfrak{a}:N(\mathfrak{a})=n}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}a\bmod-\Delta\\
\gcd(a,-\Delta)=1\end{subarray}}\chi_{q_{1}}(a)(1+\chi(a)) \displaystyle\hskip 28.45274pt\times\sum_{d\leq\max\sqrt{|F(x,y)|/n_{1}n_{2}k}}\chi(d)S(n,a,1,k,b;d)+O\left(\frac{BL^{2}}{tk^{2}}\log(B)^{\rho_{\Delta,f}-2-10^{-7}}\right). $$

Above, the maximum is taken over $(x,y)\in(B/tk)^{1/2}\mathcal{B}(\mathbf{x}_{0},L).$ For “small” moduli $d\leq D:=(B/tk)^{\deg(F)/4}(nk)^{-1/2}\log(B)^{-10^{-5}},$ we apply Proposition 9.1, our level of distribution result. From this, we can see that

$$ \sum_{d\leq D}\chi(d)S(n,a,1,k,b;d)=\frac{BL^{2}}{tk^{3}}\sum_{d\leq D}\frac{\chi(d)\varrho_{F}(d;b,n,a,1,k)}{d^{2}b^{2}n^{2}(-\Delta)^{2}}\\
+O\Bigg(\frac{\varrho_{F}(k)\tau(k)B}{\varphi(k)k^{3/2}tn^{1/2}}\log(B)^{-10^{-5}}(\log\log(B)+\log(k))+\frac{64^{\omega(k)}B}{tk^{5/2}n^{1/2}b^{2}}\log(B)^{-10^{-6}}\\
+\frac{64^{\omega(k)}BL}{tk^{7/4}}\cdot\frac{\tau(b^{4})}{b}\log(B)^{-10^{-6}}\Bigg). $$

#### Remark 11.2.

If $F(x,y)$ is an irreducible cubic form, the level of distribution error for any $D\leq(B/tk)^{3/4}(nk)^{-1/2}$ is sufficient. So, in this case we do not need to separately handle these “large” moduli.

On the other hand, Proposition 10.1 for “large” moduli tells us that

$$ \sum_{(B/tk)^{\deg(F)/4}(nk)^{-1/2}\gg d\geq D}\chi(d)S(n,a,1,k,b;d)\\
\ll\left(\frac{B}{b^{2}tk^{3/2}}+\frac{B^{3/4}\nu_{1}(k)^{1/2}}{bt^{3/4}k^{3/4}}\right)\cdot(4\deg(F))^{\omega(k)}\cdot\log(B)^{\rho_{\Delta,f}/2-1-10^{-6}}. $$

Together, this gives us that

$$ S(X_{\Delta,f},\mathcal{B}(\mathbf{x}_{0},L);q_{1},q_{2},t,k)=\frac{BL^{2}}{tk^{3}}\cdot\sum_{b\leq\log(B)^{10^{-7}}}\mu(b)\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}n\ll\log(B)^{10^{-7}}\\
p\mid n\implies p\mid-\Delta\end{subarray}}\chi_{q_{1}}(p_{q_{2}}(n))\chi_{q_{2}}(p_{q_{1}}(n))\mathbf{1}_{\exists\mathfrak{a}:N(\mathfrak{a})=n}\\
\times\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}a\bmod-\Delta\\
\gcd(a,-\Delta)=1\end{subarray}}\chi_{q_{1}}(a)(1+\chi(a))\sum_{d\leq D}\frac{\chi(d)\varrho_{F}(d;b,n,a,1,k)}{d^{2}b^{2}n^{2}(-\Delta)^{2}}\\
+O\left(64^{\omega(k)}\log(k)\cdot\left(\frac{B}{tk^{3/2}}+\frac{B^{3/4}\nu_{1}(k)^{1/2}}{t^{3/4}k^{3/4}}\right)\log(B)^{\rho_{\Delta,f}-2-10^{-7}}\right). $$

Here we have used that $n,b\leq\log(B)^{10^{-7}}$ are small constants. Note that $\rho_{\Delta,f}\geq 2$ by definition and hence $\rho_{\Delta,f}-2\geq\rho_{\Delta,f}/2-1$ .

Let us rework this main term. First, we can extend the sum over $n,b\leq\log(B)^{10^{-7}}$ to one over all $n$ and all $b$ by again bounding away the contribution from large $n$ and large $b$ with the Nair sieve (Theorem 3.11). This leaves us with the term

$$ \sum_{b}\frac{\mu(b)}{b^{2}}\sum_{d\leq D}\frac{\chi(d)\varrho_{F}(d;b,n,a,1,k)}{d^{2}n^{2}(-\Delta)^{2}}. $$

We can also use multiplicativity of $\varrho_{F}$ to write:

$$ \varrho_{F}(d;b,n,a,1,k)=\varrho_{F}(p_{\neg-\Delta}(b),kd)\varrho_{F}(p_{-\Delta}(b),n,a), $$

where we have defined:

$$ \varrho_{F}(p_{\neg-\Delta}(b),kd)=\#\{\mathbf{x}\bmod p_{\neg-\Delta}(b)kd:p_{\neg-\Delta}(b)\mid(x,y),F(x,y)\equiv 0\bmod kd\} $$

$$ \varrho_{F}(p_{-\Delta}(b),n,a)=\#\{\mathbf{x}\bmod p_{-\Delta}(b)n(-\Delta):p_{-\Delta}(b)\mid(x,y),p_{-\Delta}(F(x,y))=n,p_{\neg-\Delta}(F(x,y))\equiv a\bmod-\Delta\}. $$

Note that we have used that $\gcd(k,-\Delta)=1$ by construction and $\gcd(d,-\Delta)=1$ for those $d$ with nonzero contribution to the sum. Let us use the notation that $b=b_{\neg-\Delta}b_{-\Delta}$ where $\gcd(b_{\neg-\Delta},-\Delta)=1$ and $p\mid b_{-\Delta}\implies p\mid-\Delta$ . Consequently, the main term can be rewritten as:

$$ \frac{BL^{2}}{tk^{3}}\cdot\bigtriangledown_{q_{1},q_{2}}\cdot V(k,D), $$

where we define:

$$ \bigtriangledown_{q_{1},q_{2}}:=\sum_{b_{-\Delta}}\frac{\mu(b_{-\Delta})}{b_{-\Delta}^{2}}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}p\mid n\implies p\mid-\Delta\end{subarray}}\frac{\chi_{q_{1}}(p_{q_{2}}(n))\chi_{q_{2}}(p_{q_{2}}(n))\mathbf{1}_{\exists\mathfrak{a}:N(\mathfrak{a})=n}}{n^{2}}\\
\times\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}a\bmod-\Delta\\
\gcd(a,-\Delta)=1\end{subarray}}\frac{\chi_{q_{1}}(a)(1+\chi(a))}{(-\Delta)^{2}}\cdot\varrho_{F}(b_{-\Delta},n,a). $$

$$ V(k,D)=\sum_{b_{\neg-\Delta}}\frac{\mu(b_{\neg-\Delta})}{b_{\neg-\Delta}^{2}}\sum_{d\leq D}\frac{\chi(d)\varrho_{F}(b_{\neg-\Delta},kd)}{d^{2}}. $$

Observe that the sum over $b_{\neg-\Delta}$ converges absolutely above in $V(k,D)$ . Both the terms $\bigtriangledown_{q_{1},q_{2}}$ and $V(k,D)$ will be generalized in the more complicated cases below; however, we can immediately rearrange $\bigtriangledown_{q_{1},q_{2}}$ into a less complicated expression.

Noting that for $\mu(b_{-\Delta})$ to be nonzero, $b_{-\Delta}$ must be squarefree and hence divides $-\Delta$ . Hence, we can rewrite:

$$ \displaystyle\bigtriangledown_{q_{1},q_{2}} \displaystyle=\sum_{p\mid n\implies p\mid-\Delta}\frac{\chi_{q_{1}}(p_{q_{2}}(n))\chi_{q_{2}}(p_{q_{2}}(n))\mathbf{1}_{\exists\mathfrak{a}:N(\mathfrak{a})=n}}{n^{2}} \displaystyle\hskip 28.45274pt\times\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}a\bmod-\Delta\\
\gcd(a,-\Delta)=1\end{subarray}}\frac{\chi_{q_{1}}(a)+\chi_{q_{2}}(a)}{(-\Delta)^{2}}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}\mathbf{x}\bmod n(-\Delta)^{2}\\
p_{-\Delta}(F(x,y))=n\\
p_{\neg-\Delta}(F(x,y))\equiv a\bmod-\Delta\end{subarray}}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}b\mid x,y\\
b\mid-\Delta\end{subarray}}\frac{\mu(b)}{b^{2}}\cdot\left(\frac{b}{-\Delta}\right)^{2} \displaystyle=\sum_{p\mid n\implies p\mid-\Delta}\frac{\chi_{q_{1}}(p_{q_{2}}(n))\chi_{q_{2}}(p_{q_{2}}(n))\mathbf{1}_{\exists\mathfrak{a}:N(\mathfrak{a})=n}}{n^{2}}\times\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}a\bmod-\Delta\\
\gcd(a,-\Delta)=1\end{subarray}}\frac{\chi_{q_{1}}(a)+\chi_{q_{2}}(a)}{(-\Delta)^{2}}\varrho_{F}^{*}(n,a), $$

where we use Möbius inversion on the sum over $b$ and hence

$$ \varrho_{F}^{*}(n,a)=\#\{\mathbf{x}\bmod n(-\Delta):\gcd(x,y,-\Delta)=1,p_{-\Delta}(F(x,y))=n,p_{\neg-\Delta}(F(x,y))\equiv a\bmod-\Delta\}. $$

We can also rearrange the sum over $b$ for $V(k,D)$ :

$$ V(k,D)=\sum_{d\leq D}\frac{\chi(d)}{d^{2}}\sum_{\gcd(b_{\neg-\Delta},-\Delta)=1}\frac{\mu(b_{\neg-\Delta})}{b_{\neg-\Delta}^{2}}\cdot\varrho_{F}(b_{\neg-\Delta},kd)\\
=\sum_{d\leq D}\frac{\chi(d)}{d^{2}}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}\mathbf{x}_{0}\bmod kd\\
kd\mid F(\mathbf{x}_{0})\end{subarray}}\sum_{\gcd(b_{\neg-\Delta},-\Delta)=1}\frac{\mu(b_{\neg-\Delta})}{b_{\neg-\Delta}^{2}}\cdot\#\{\mathbf{x}\bmod b_{\neg-\Delta}kd:b_{\neg-\Delta}\mid\gcd(x,y),\mathbf{x}\equiv\mathbf{x}_{0}\bmod kd\}. $$

This local count can be determined precisely:

$$ \#\{\mathbf{x}\bmod b_{\neg-\Delta}kd:b_{\neg-\Delta}\mid\gcd(x,y),\mathbf{x}\equiv\mathbf{x}_{0}\bmod kd\}=\begin{cases}b^{\prime 2},&b^{\prime}\mid\gcd(kd,b_{\neg-\Delta}),b^{\prime}\mid\mathbf{x}_{0},\\
1,&\text{otherwise.}\end{cases} $$

Consequently, we see that

$$ \sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}\mathbf{x}_{0}\bmod kd\\
kd\mid F(\mathbf{x}_{0})\end{subarray}}\sum_{\gcd(b_{\neg-\Delta},-\Delta)=1}\frac{\mu(b_{\neg-\Delta})}{b_{\neg-\Delta}^{2}}\cdot\#\{\mathbf{x}\bmod b_{\neg-\Delta}kd:b_{\neg-\Delta}\mid\gcd(x,y),\mathbf{x}\equiv\mathbf{x}_{0}\bmod kd\}\\
=\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}\mathbf{x}_{0}\bmod kd\\
kd\mid F(\mathbf{x}_{0})\end{subarray}}\prod_{p\mid-\Delta}\left(1-p^{-2}\cdot\begin{cases}p^{2},&p\mid kd,p\mid\mathbf{x}_{0},\\
0,&p\mid kd,p\nmid\mathbf{x}_{0},\\
1,&p\nmid kd,\end{cases}\right)=\prod_{p\nmid kd(-\Delta)}\left(1-\frac{1}{p^{2}}\right)\varrho_{F}^{*}(kd). $$

Hence, we have that

$$ V(k,D)=\sum_{d\leq D}\frac{\chi(d)\varrho_{F}^{*}(kd)}{d^{2}}\prod_{p\nmid kd(-\Delta)}\left(1-\frac{1}{p^{2}}\right)=\prod_{p\nmid-\Delta}\left(1-\frac{1}{p^{2}}\right)\sum_{d\leq D}\prod_{p\mid kd}\left(1-\frac{1}{p^{2}}\right)^{-1}\frac{\chi(d)\varrho_{F}^{*}(kd)}{d^{2}}. $$

#### 11.1.2. $F(x,y)$ is the product of two irreducible factors

Write $F(x,y)=F_{1}(x,y)F_{2}(x,y)$ as the decomposition of $F(x,y)$ into irreducible factors. If one of the factors is linear, assume without loss of generality that it is $F_{1}$ . Following the reductions of §8, we have that:

$$ \displaystyle S(X_{\Delta,f},\mathcal{B}(\mathbf{x}_{0},L);q_{1},q_{2},t,k)=\sum_{c\mid\textrm{Res}(F_{1},F_{2})}\mu(c)\chi(c)S(\mathbf{c}=(c,c),\mathbf{k}) \displaystyle=\sum_{c\mid\textrm{Res}(F_{1},F_{2})}\mu(c)\chi(c)\times\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}n\ll\log(B)^{10^{-7}}\\
p\mid n\implies p\mid-\Delta\end{subarray}}\chi_{q_{1}}(p_{q_{2}}(n))\chi_{q_{2}}(p_{q_{1}}(n))\mathbf{1}_{\exists\mathfrak{a}:N(\mathfrak{a})=n}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}\mathbf{a}\bmod-\Delta\\
\gcd(a_{i},-\Delta)=1\end{subarray}}\chi_{q_{1}}(a)S(n,\mathbf{a},\mathbf{c},\mathbf{k}) \displaystyle\hskip 142.26378pt+O\left(\frac{BL^{2}}{tk^{2}}\log(B)^{\rho_{\Delta,f}-2-10^{-7}}\right) \displaystyle=\sum_{c\mid\textrm{Res}(F_{1},F_{2})}\mu(c)\chi(c)\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}n\ll\log(B)^{10^{-7}}\\
p\mid n\implies p\mid-\Delta\end{subarray}}\chi_{q_{1}}(p_{q_{2}}(n))\chi_{q_{2}}(p_{q_{1}}(n))\mathbf{1}_{\exists\mathfrak{a}:N(\mathfrak{a})=n}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}\mathbf{a}\bmod-\Delta\\
\gcd(a_{i},-\Delta)=1\end{subarray}}\chi_{q_{1}}(a) \displaystyle\hskip 56.9055pt\times\sum_{b\leq\log(B)^{10^{-7}}}\mu(b)S(n,\mathbf{a},\mathbf{c},\mathbf{k};b)+O\left(\frac{BL^{2}}{tk^{2}}\log(B)^{\rho_{\Delta,f}-2-10^{-7}}\right) \displaystyle=\sum_{c\mid\textrm{Res}(F_{1},F_{2})}\mu(c)\chi(c)\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}n\ll\log(B)^{10^{-7}}\\
p\mid n\implies p\mid-\Delta\end{subarray}}\chi_{q_{1}}(p_{q_{2}}(n))\chi_{q_{2}}(p_{q_{1}}(n))\mathbf{1}_{\exists\mathfrak{a}:N(\mathfrak{a})=n}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}\mathbf{a}\bmod-\Delta\\
\gcd(a_{i},-\Delta)=1\end{subarray}}\chi_{q_{1}}(a)(1+\chi(a_{1}))(1+\chi(a_{2})) \displaystyle\hskip 56.9055pt\times\sum_{b\leq\log(B)^{10^{-7}}}\mu(b)\sum_{d_{i}\leq\max\sqrt{|F_{i}(x,y)|/n_{i}k_{i}}}\chi(d)S(n,\mathbf{a},\mathbf{c},\mathbf{k},b;\mathbf{d}) \displaystyle\hskip 170.71652pt+O\left(\frac{BL^{2}}{tk^{2}}\log(B)^{\rho_{\Delta,f}-2-10^{-7}}\right). $$

If $F_{1}$ and $F_{2}$ are both irreducible quadratics, we write that $\mathbf{d}\leq\mathbf{D}$ if $\mathbf{d}=(d_{1},d_{2})$ satisfies that $d_{1}d_{2}\leq D:=(B/tk)^{\deg(F)/4}(nk)^{-1/2}\log(B)^{-10^{-5}}$ . If $F_{1}$ is linear, we define $D_{1}:=(B/tk)^{1/4}(n_{1}k_{1})^{-1/2}\log(B)^{-2-10^{-5}}$ . We write $\mathbf{d}\leq\mathbf{D}$ when $d_{1}\leq D_{1}$ – for such vectors $\mathbf{d}$ , we automatically have that $d\leq(B/tk)^{\deg(F)/4}(nk)^{-1/2}\log(B)^{-2-10^{-5}}.$ Proposition 9.1 tells us that for $\mathbf{d}\leq\mathbf{D}$ , we have that:

$$ \sum_{d_{i}\leq D_{i}}\chi(d)S(n,\mathbf{a},\mathbf{c},\mathbf{k},b;\mathbf{d})=\frac{BL^{2}}{tk^{3}}\cdot\sum_{\mathbf{d}\leq\mathbf{D}}\frac{\chi(d)\varrho_{F}(\mathbf{d};b,n,\mathbf{a},\mathbf{c},\mathbf{k})}{c^{2}d^{2}b^{2}n^{2}(-\Delta)^{2}}\\
+O\Bigg(\frac{\varrho_{F}(k)\tau(k)B}{t\varphi(k)k^{3/2}n^{1/2}}\log(B)^{-10^{-5}}(\log\log(B)+\log(k))+\frac{64^{\omega(k)}B}{tk^{5/2}n^{1/2}b^{2}}\log(B)^{-10^{-6}}\\
+\frac{64^{\omega(k)}BL}{tk^{7/4}}\cdot\frac{\tau(b^{4})}{b}\cdot\log(B)^{-10^{-6}}+\frac{B^{3/4}L}{(tk)^{3/4}(k_{1}n_{1})^{1/2}b}\log(B)^{-10^{-6}}\Bigg). $$

Note that this last term does not exist when $F_{1}(x,y)$ and $F_{2}(x,y)$ are both irreducible quadratics. Also we observe an abuse of notation above – here $c$ denotes the product of the entries of the vector $\mathbf{c}$ compared to the entries of the vector earlier on this page.

Applying either Proposition 10.1 (if $F_{1},F_{2}$ are both quadratic) or Proposition 10.2 (if $F_{1}$ or $F_{2}$ is linear), we achieve the upper bound:

$$ \sum_{\mathbf{d}\not\leq\mathbf{D}}\chi(d)S(n,\mathbf{a},\mathbf{c},\mathbf{k},b;\mathbf{d})\ll\frac{B(16\deg(F))^{\omega(k)}}{tk^{2}}\cdot\log(B/tk)^{\rho_{\Delta,f}-2-10^{-5}}\\
+\left(\frac{B}{b^{2}tk^{3/2}}+\frac{B^{3/4}\nu_{1}(k)^{1/2}}{bt^{3/4}k^{3/4}}\right)\cdot(4\deg(F))^{\omega(k)}\cdot\log(B)^{\rho_{\Delta,f}/2-1-10^{-6}}. $$

Here we have used that $0\leq\rho_{\Delta,f}/2-1\leq\rho_{\Delta,f}-2.$

Recalling that $n,b\leq\log(B)^{10^{-7}}$ , we get the estimate:

$$ S(X_{\Delta,f},\mathcal{B}(\mathbf{x}_{0},L);q_{1},q_{2},t,k)=\frac{BL^{2}}{tk^{3}}\cdot C_{q_{1},q_{2},f,k}(B/tk)\cdot(1+O(\log(B)^{-10^{-7}}))\\
+O\left(\frac{64^{\omega(k)}\log(k)B}{tk^{3/2}}\log(B)^{\rho_{\Delta,f}-2-10^{-7}}+\frac{B^{3/4}\cdot((4\deg(F))^{\omega(k)}\nu_{1}(k)^{1/2}+L)}{(tk)^{3/4}}\cdot\log(B)^{-10^{-7}}\right), $$

where we define:

$$ C_{q_{1},q_{2},f,k}(B/tk):=\sum_{c^{\prime}\mid\textrm{Res}(F_{1},F_{2})}\frac{\mu(c^{\prime})\chi(c^{\prime})}{(c^{\prime})^{4}}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}p\mid n\implies p\mid\Delta\end{subarray}}\frac{\chi_{q_{1}}(p_{q_{2}}(n))\chi_{q_{2}}(p_{q_{1}}(n))\mathbf{1}_{\exists\mathfrak{a}:N(\mathfrak{a})=n}}{n^{2}}\\
\times\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}\mathbf{a}\bmod\Delta\\
\gcd(a_{i},\Delta)=1\end{subarray}}\frac{\chi_{q_{1}}(a)(1+\chi(a_{1}))(1+\chi(a_{2}))}{(-\Delta)^{2}}\sum_{b}\frac{\mu(b)}{b^{2}}\sum_{\mathbf{d}\leq\mathbf{D}}\frac{\chi(d)\varrho_{F}(\mathbf{d};b,n,\mathbf{a},\mathbf{c},\mathbf{k})}{d^{2}}. $$

It is of note here that our abusive notation has come back to bite us – indeed, in this situation $\mathbf{c}=(c^{\prime},c^{\prime})$ and hence $c=(c^{\prime})^{2}$ (in previous reductions, we used the letter $c$ to denote the variable $c^{\prime}$ above).

Now, we generalize the definitions of $\bigtriangledown_{q_{1},q_{2}}$ and $V(k,D)$ from before (in (11.1), (11.2)).

#### Definition 11.3.

We define the constant:

$$ \bigtriangledown_{q_{1},q_{2}}(\mathbf{c}):=\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}p\mid n\implies p\mid-\Delta\end{subarray}}\frac{\chi_{q_{1}}(p_{q_{2}}(n))\chi_{q_{2}}(p_{q_{1}}(n))\mathbf{1}_{\exists\mathfrak{a}:N(\mathfrak{a})=n}}{n^{2}}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}\mathbf{a}\bmod-\Delta\\
\gcd(a_{i},-\Delta)=1\end{subarray}}\frac{\chi_{q_{1}}(a)}{(-\Delta)^{2}}\times\prod_{i=1}^{r}(1+\chi(a_{i}))\varrho_{F}^{*}(n,\mathbf{c}\mathbf{a}). $$

Here the function $\varrho_{f}(n,\mathbf{a})$ denotes:

#### Definition 11.4.

$$ V(\mathbf{c},\mathbf{k},D):=\prod_{p\nmid-\Delta}\left(1-\frac{1}{p^{2}}\right)\sum_{\mathbf{d}\leq\mathbf{D}}\frac{\chi(d)\varrho_{F}^{*}(\mathbf{c}\mathbf{k}\mathbf{d})}{d^{2}}\prod_{p\mid cdk}\left(1-\frac{1}{p^{2}}\right)^{-1}, $$

$$ \varrho_{F}(\mathbf{d};b,n,\mathbf{a},\mathbf{c},\mathbf{k})=\varrho_{F}(p_{-\Delta}(b),n,\mathbf{c}\mathbf{a})\varrho_{F}(p_{\neg-\Delta}(b),\mathbf{c}\mathbf{k}\mathbf{d}),. $$

#### 11.1.5. Completion of the proof of Proposition 8.1

Noting that $\bigtriangledown_{q_{1},q_{2}}(\mathbf{c})$ is a finite constant, and since $F(x,y)$ is a squarefree form we know that the sum over $\mathbf{c}$ is given by a finite sum, we see that in order to establish Proposition 8.1 it suffices to prove that for any fixed $\mathbf{c}$ we have that:

$$ V(\mathbf{c},\mathbf{k},D)=c_{q_{1},q_{2},f,k,\mathbf{c}}\log(B/tk)^{\rho_{\Delta,f}-2}(1+O(\log(B)^{-1/2})). $$

To do so, it suffices to understand the growth of the factor:

$$ \sum_{\mathbf{d}\leq\mathbf{D}}\frac{\chi(d)\varrho_{F}^{*}(\mathbf{c}\mathbf{k}\mathbf{d})}{d^{2}}\prod_{p\mid ckd}\left(1-\frac{1}{p^{2}}\right)^{-1}. $$

Let us define the Dirichlet series:

$$ \xi(s;F,\chi,\mathbf{c},\mathbf{k})=\sum_{\mathbf{d}}\frac{\chi(d)\varrho_{F}^{*}(\mathbf{c}\mathbf{k}\mathbf{d})}{d^{2s}}\prod_{p\mid ckd}\left(1-\frac{1}{p^{2}}\right)^{-1}. $$

Since $\varrho_{F}^{*}(n)\leq\deg(F)^{\omega(n)}n$ for all but finitely many values of $n$ , we can see that the above Dirichlet series converges for $\Re(s)>1.$ Moreover, for $\Re(s)>1$ , we have the Euler product expansion:

$$ \xi(s;F,\chi,\mathbf{c},\mathbf{k})=\mathfrak{S}_{\mathbf{c},\mathbf{k}}^{\prime}(s)\prod_{p\nmid ck}\left(1+(1-p^{-2})^{-1}\cdot\left(\frac{\chi(p)}{p^{2s}}\cdot(\varrho_{F}^{*}((p,1,...,1))+\ldots+\varrho_{F}^{*}((1,...,p)))+\frac{\chi(p)^{2}}{p^{4s}}\cdot\ldots\right)\right), $$

where we define:

$$ \mathfrak{S}_{\mathbf{c},\mathbf{k}}^{\prime}(s):=\prod_{\begin{subarray}{c}p\mid ck\\
p^{e_{i}}\|c_{i}k_{i}\end{subarray}}(1-p^{-2})^{-1}\cdot\left(\varrho_{F}^{*}((p^{e_{1}},...,p^{e_{r}}))+\frac{\chi(p)}{p^{2s}}\cdot(\varrho_{F}^{*}((p^{e_{1}+1},...,p^{e_{r}}))+\ldots+\varrho_{F}^{*}((p^{e_{1}},...,p^{e_{r}+1})))+\ldots\right). $$

Note that this product is over a finite number of primes (depending on $\mathbf{c}$ and $\mathbf{k}$ ) and hence converges. The local factors at $p\nmid ck$ are close to those in the Euler product expansion of $\xi(s;F,\chi)$ (as defined in (3.2)): in particular, we know that for such primes $\varrho_{F}^{*}((p,1,\dots,1))+\dots\varrho_{F}^{*}((1,\dots,p))=\varrho_{F}^{*}(p)$ . So, the local factors are equivalent up to a factor of $O(p^{-2s-1}+p^{-4s+2}).$ Thus, we get that for $\Re(s)>1$ ,

$$ \xi(s;F,\chi,\mathbf{c},\mathbf{k})=\mathfrak{S}_{\mathbf{c},\mathbf{k}}(s)\cdot\mathfrak{S}_{F}(s)\cdot\xi(s;F,\chi), $$

where we take:

$$ \mathfrak{S}_{\mathbf{c},\mathbf{k}}(s):=\mathfrak{S}_{\mathbf{c},\mathbf{k}}^{\prime}(s)\cdot\prod_{p\mid ck}\left(1+\frac{\chi(p)}{p^{2s}}\cdot(\varrho_{F}^{*}((p,1,...,1))+\ldots+\varrho_{F}^{*}((1,...,p)))+\frac{\chi(p)^{2}}{p^{4s}}\cdot\ldots\right)^{-1}, $$

and $\mathfrak{S}_{F}(s)$ converges absolutely for $\Re(s)>3/4$ .

By Lemma 3.15, we can see that $\xi(s;F,\chi,\mathbf{c},\mathbf{k})$ will have a meromorphic continuation to $\Re(s)>1/2$ and a pole of order $\rho_{\Delta,f}-2$ at $s=1$ . Thus, we have that:

$$ V(\mathbf{c},\mathbf{k},D)=\sum_{\mathbf{d}\leq\mathbf{D}}\frac{\chi(d)\varrho_{F}^{*}(\mathbf{c}\mathbf{k}\mathbf{d})}{d^{2}}\prod_{p\mid ckd}\left(1-\frac{1}{p^{2}}\right)^{-1}\\
=\mathfrak{S}_{\mathbf{c},\mathbf{k}}(1)\mathfrak{S}_{F}(1)\textrm{Res}_{s=1}\xi(s;F,\chi)\cdot\log(D)^{\rho_{\Delta,f}-2}(1+O(\log(D)^{-1})). $$

Recalling that $D=(B/tk)^{\deg(F)/4}k^{-1/2}\log(B)^{-\varepsilon}$ , where $\varepsilon=10^{-5}$ if there are no linear factors and $\varepsilon=-2-10^{-5}$ if $F$ has linear factors, we establish the claim (11.6) for a fixed value of $k$ and $\mathbf{c}$ :

$$ V(\mathbf{c},\mathbf{k},D)=c_{q_{1},q_{2},f,k,\mathbf{c}}\log(B/tk)^{\rho_{\Delta,f}-2}(1+O(\log(B)^{-1/2})), $$

where $c_{q_{1},q_{2},f,k,\mathbf{c}}=\mathfrak{S}_{\mathbf{c},\mathbf{k}}(1)\mathfrak{S}_{F}(1)\cdot\textrm{Res}_{s=1}\xi(s;F,\chi)\cdot(\deg(F)/4)^{\rho_{\Delta,f}-2}.$ ∎
